title: 2026 Series Champions Update + World Finals Preview
text: Two national titles are settled. The World of Outlaws crown comes down to four nights at Charlotte. High Limit Racing: Rico Abreu Rico Abreu clinched the 2026 High Limit Racing championship at the season finale at Texas Motor Speedway, where Giovanni Scelzi won the feature. Read…
body: Two national titles are settled. The World of Outlaws crown comes down to four nights at Charlotte. High Limit Racing: Rico Abreu Rico Abreu clinched the 2026 High Limit Racing championship at the season finale at Texas Motor Speedway, where Giovanni Scelzi won the feature. Read our finale recap . USAC National Sprint Car: Kyle Cummins Kyle Cummins locked up his second straight USAC AMSOIL National Sprint Car title at Central Arizona Raceway with two races left. He finished with 3,333 points, a career-high 11 wins, 351 laps led and 45 top-10s in 48 starts in the Petty Performance Racing No. 3p. World of Outlaws: Gravel leads into Charlotte David Gravel heads to the World Finals with a 124-point lead: 9,732 to Michael “Buddy” Kofoid’s 9,608. Sheldon Haudenschild is third, 222 back. Gravel is not mathematically locked in, but solid finishes at Charlotte would clinch it. Photo: Tyler Carr / World Racing Group The Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals runs Nov. 4–7 at The Dirt Track at Charlotte in Concord, N.C. World of Outlaws Sprint Cars, World of Outlaws Late Models and the Super DIRTcar Series share the bill. Thursday’s program was moved up one hour because of a rain threat: opening ceremonies at 2:50 p.m. ET and racing at 3 p.m.; the midway Fan Zone still opens at 12 p.m. Friday and Saturday opening ceremonies remain at 4 p.m. ET. Photo: Tyler Carr / World Racing Group

title: Silly season 2027: Will World of Outlaws drivers move to High Limit?
text: Brady Bacon is locked into the Vermeer 55 for 2027, and the bigger question is whether any World of Outlaws drivers follow him to High Limit. Silly season is starting, and the question people in the pits are asking is simple: will any World of Outlaws drivers make the move to…
body: Brady Bacon is locked into the Vermeer 55 for 2027, and the bigger question is whether any World of Outlaws drivers follow him to High Limit. Silly season is starting, and the question people in the pits are asking is simple: will any World of Outlaws drivers make the move to High Limit in 2027? Rumors are circulating about major changes ahead. So far, very little is confirmed. Tanner Holmes and Justin Peck are confirmed to return to High Limit in 2027. So is the Vermeer 55 team, with crew chief Tye Wolfgang back on the box. All of it was announced at the High Limit banquet the weekend of October 17 and 18. Update, October 29: The Vermeer 55 seat is filled. On October 22, team owner Tony Vermeer named Brady Bacon the full-time driver of the No. 55 for the 2027 High Limit season, with Tye Wolfgang staying on as crew chief. Bacon drove the car for the final 10 races of 2026, including a podium at Lakeside Speedway and a top five at Eldora Speedway. The four-time USAC National Sprint Car champion has 64 USAC national sprint car wins, second all-time. 2027 will be his first full-time season in a winged 410 sprint car, though he ran the winged 360 ASCS National Tour full-time from 2010 to 2012 and won 12 races. He is eligible for High Limit Rookie of the Year. The questions to follow over the winter: Does a World of Outlaws regular make the jump to High Limit? Do other teams reshuffle once the first announcements land? Until teams and series confirm their plans, treat everything beyond the names above as rumor. We will update this page as announcements come in.

text: Rico Abreu was honored as the 2026 Interstate Batteries High Limit Racing champion in Fort Worth, Texas, finishing 31 points ahead of Giovanni Scelzi, per Dirt Track Digest. Rico Abreu was honored at the Interstate Batteries High Limit Racing Championship Awards Celebration in…
body: Rico Abreu was honored as the 2026 Interstate Batteries High Limit Racing champion in Fort Worth, Texas, finishing 31 points ahead of Giovanni Scelzi, per Dirt Track Digest. Rico Abreu was honored at the Interstate Batteries High Limit Racing Championship Awards Celebration in Fort Worth. He edged Giovanni Scelzi by 31 points after a 54-race season across 19 states. It is Abreu's second straight High Limit title. Tanner Holmes received Most Improved among other awards. High Roller Club teams received more than $3 million in postseason money in addition to race purses.

title: Rico Abreu Sweeps World Finals Qualifying Night at Charlotte
text: Rico Abreu set overall Simpson Quick Time for Thursday and Friday heat lineups Wednesday night at the Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. More than 40 competitors signed in for the World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series…
body: Rico Abreu set overall Simpson Quick Time for Thursday and Friday heat lineups Wednesday night at the Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. More than 40 competitors signed in for the World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series season sendoff at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. Wednesday’s Honest Abe Roofing Qualifying sessions set heat race lineups for Thursday and Friday. Feature points accumulated over those two nights will set heats for Saturday’s $25,000-to-win season finale. David Gravel topped Flight A for Thursday’s program in the Big Game Motorsports No. 2 with a 12.688. Rico Abreu, in the Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing No. 14, set overall Simpson Quick Time with a 12.584 in Flight B. Bill Balog, Buddy Schweibinz, Tyler Courtney and Anthony Macri completed Thursday Flight A’s top five. Michael “Buddy” Kofoid, Garet Williamson, Tanner Holmes and Sheldon Haudenschild rounded out Flight B’s top five behind Abreu. Abreu also paced Friday Flight A with a 12.542, sweeping both Simpson Quick Time awards. Sheldon Haudenschild led Friday Flight B at 12.678 in the KCP Racing/NOS Energy Drink Grand Prix Guava No. 18. Buddy Schweibinz, Bill Balog, Giovanni Scelzi and Parker Price-Miller completed Friday Flight A’s top five after Abreu. Cameron Smith, Tanner Holmes, Matt Farnham and Carson Macedo rounded out Flight B behind Haudenschild. Separately, World of Outlaws announced that Thursday’s World Finals program has been moved up one hour because of a rain threat. Opening ceremonies are scheduled for 2:50 p.m. ET, with racing at 3 p.m. Friday and Saturday programs remain unchanged.

title: Rico Abreu Wins Thursday World Finals Feature at Charlotte
text: Rico Abreu started third and won Thursday’s 25-lap NOS Energy Drink feature at the Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. Tyler Courtney finished second and Bill Balog third. Rico Abreu followed his qualifying sweep with a feature win…
body: Rico Abreu started third and won Thursday’s 25-lap NOS Energy Drink feature at the Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. Tyler Courtney finished second and Bill Balog third. Rico Abreu followed his qualifying sweep with a feature win Thursday at Charlotte. Abreu, in the Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing No. 14, started third in the 25-lap World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series main and finished ahead of Tyler Courtney and Bill Balog. Michael “Buddy” Kofoid ran fourth from sixth and Garet Williamson finished fifth after starting on the pole. David Gravel was sixth from fifth. Abreu set the night up earlier in the program. He won the WIX Filters heat from the front row and finished third in the six-lap Toyota Dash, which Williamson won over Balog. Courtney started fourth in the feature after finishing fourth in the dash. The other heat winners were Gravel, Balog and Kofoid. Logan Schuchart, Giovanni Scelzi, Logan Rumsey (from 16th) and Spencer Bayston (from 15th) completed the top 10. Parker Price-Miller won the Last Chance Showdown and Emerson Axsom won the C-main. Conner Morrell, Buddy Schweibinz, Sheldon Haudenschild and Skylar Gee were listed as DNFs. Abreu came to Charlotte off the 2026 High Limit Racing championship. On Wednesday’s qualifying night he set overall Simpson Quick Time for both Thursday (12.584) and Friday (12.542) heat lineups. Gravel came into the week going for a third straight World of Outlaws title with Big Game Motorsports. Feature points from Thursday and Friday will set heat races for Saturday’s $25,000-to-win season finale. Balog led 21 of the 25 laps on the cushion before Abreu got a run off the bottom of Turn 2 with fewer than five laps left and drove by for the lead, according to World of Outlaws. Abreu led the final four laps and won by 1.136 seconds over Courtney, earning $15,000. World of Outlaws said the win was Abreu’s 11th sprint car victory of 2026 and his second at Charlotte, and the 332nd World of Outlaws win for Tony Stewart’s operation, 14 of them at the Concord track. The World Finals continue Friday with another $15,000-to-win sprint car program.

title: Jonathan Allard Wins Second Baypark Sprint Car Feature of the Season
text: Former two-time New Zealand Sprint Car champion Jonathan Allard led from start to finish in the 20-lap feature at Baypark Speedway, holding off a late charge from Ryan O’Connor to claim his second win of the young season. Jonathan Allard, the Auckland-based California racer and…
body: Former two-time New Zealand Sprint Car champion Jonathan Allard led from start to finish in the 20-lap feature at Baypark Speedway, holding off a late charge from Ryan O’Connor to claim his second win of the young season. Jonathan Allard, the Auckland-based California racer and two-time New Zealand champion, continued his strong start to the 2026-27 season by leading wire-to-wire in the Sprint Car feature at Baypark Speedway’s fireworks meeting. O’Connor closed to within 0.643 seconds at the finish. The result builds on Allard’s season-opening win at the same track and sets an early marker ahead of the New Zealand Sprint Car Championship in March.

title: Anthony Macri Wins York Excavating Sprint Showdown at BAPS Motor Speedway
text: Macri started on the pole in the No. 39M and beat Chase Dietz and Ryan Smith in the 30-lap, $10,000-to-win feature at York Haven, Pa., on Saturday, Nov. 14. Anthony Macri won the 30-lap 410 sprint car feature at the 16th annual York Excavating Sprint Showdown at BAPS Motor…
body: Macri started on the pole in the No. 39M and beat Chase Dietz and Ryan Smith in the 30-lap, $10,000-to-win feature at York Haven, Pa., on Saturday, Nov. 14. Anthony Macri won the 30-lap 410 sprint car feature at the 16th annual York Excavating Sprint Showdown at BAPS Motor Speedway in York Haven, Pennsylvania, on Saturday, Nov. 14, according to official results posted by the track. Macri started on the pole in the No. 39M and finished ahead of Chase Dietz, Ryan Smith, Logan Rumsey and Dylan Norris. The race paid $10,000 to win and $600 to start, according to the BAPS event page. Hoseheads.com’s preview of the event described the Sprint Showdown as the final 410 sprint car race of the year on the East Coast. BAPS listed 18 entries in the 410 division. Troy Wagaman Jr. finished sixth after starting 16th, the biggest gain in the field. Lance Dewease, Cameron Smith, Brock Zearfoss and Danny Dietrich completed the top 10. Cole Dewease and Buddy Schweibinz did not finish. Qualifying ran in two groups. Dietz set the fastest time of the night at 13.835 seconds in the second group, and Macri led the first group at 14.165 seconds, according to the official results. Ryan Smith and Rumsey won the two 10-lap heat races, and every car in the 410 division transferred to the feature. Macri passed Smith for the lead on lap 13 in turn 2 while Dietz moved into second, according to a race report published by Les Gars de Courses. That report said a caution for Brent Shearer with four laps remaining set up a single-file restart, and Macri held off Dietz the rest of the way. Hoseheads.com noted before the race that Dietz entered the weekend leading the nation in sprint car feature wins and that Dietrich was a three-time Sprint Showdown winner.

title: ASCS Crowns Six 2026 Region Champions
text: Bryant Wiedeman, Cody Gardner, Jack Thomas, Kelly Miller, Bradley Fezard and Bryan Gossel won the six American Sprint Car Series regional titles in 2026, the series announced. The American Sprint Car Series named its six 2026 region champions on Friday, Nov. 20: Bryant Wiedeman…
body: Bryant Wiedeman, Cody Gardner, Jack Thomas, Kelly Miller, Bradley Fezard and Bryan Gossel won the six American Sprint Car Series regional titles in 2026, the series announced. The American Sprint Car Series named its six 2026 region champions on Friday, Nov. 20: Bryant Wiedeman (Gunsmoke Region), Cody Gardner (Hurricane Area Super Sprints), Jack Thomas (Malvern Bank Midwest Region), Kelly Miller (Northern Plains Region), Bradley Fezard (Sooner Region) and Bryan Gossel (Western Plains Region), according to an ASCS release by Matt Skipper. Wiedeman, 21, won the first title in the Gunsmoke Region’s inaugural season, ASCS said. He finished in the top 10 in all five starts, with three podiums and no finish worse than sixth. Gardner, 40, of Benton, Arkansas, won eight features in his first HASS season, with 13 top-fives and top-10s in all 14 events. ASCS said it was his first winged sprint car title and his second ASCS title, after the 2023 Elite Non-Wing season. Thomas, 17, of Bates City, Missouri, won the Midwest Region title in the region’s first season since 2014, his first full-time season in a 360, with five top-10s and two top-fives in eight races, according to the release. Miller, of Lethbridge, Alberta, won four Northern Plains features, at El Paso County, Sweetwater, Black Hills and Gillette Thunder Speedway. ASCS said it was his seventh Northern Plains campaign and that he won the 2025 Frontier Region title. Fezard, of Bonnerdale, Arkansas, won the Sooner Region title without a feature win in seven starts, ASCS said. Gossel, 50, of Windsor, Colorado, won his second straight Western Plains title with two feature wins at El Paso County, five top-fives and six top-10s in eight races, and finished 33 points ahead of Blair Cooper.

text: The 64th Nutrend Homes Australian Sprintcar Championship runs Nov. 20-21 at Hi-Tec Oils Toowoomba Speedway, the first time in 50 years the national title has been held there. The 64th Nutrend Homes Australian Sprintcar Championship is scheduled for Friday and Saturday, Nov.…
body: The 64th Nutrend Homes Australian Sprintcar Championship runs Nov. 20-21 at Hi-Tec Oils Toowoomba Speedway, the first time in 50 years the national title has been held there. The 64th Nutrend Homes Australian Sprintcar Championship is scheduled for Friday and Saturday, Nov. 20-21, at Hi-Tec Oils Toowoomba Speedway in Charlton, Queensland. The track’s official ticketing information says the national title is coming to Toowoomba for the first time in 50 years. Tasmanian Jock Goodyer is the reigning Australian No. 1. A prelude meeting is set for Wednesday, Nov. 18, with sprint cars and speedcars. Championship Night 1 on Friday also includes V8 Dirt Modifieds, and Night 2 on Saturday adds Lightning Sprints as well. The track lists Sunday, Nov. 22, as a rain date. Its official ticketing sheet lists Thursday, Nov. 19, as an off day, with no practice or calcutta. Clay-Per-View is offering a superpass covering the prelude and both championship nights. The stream is sold separately from the service’s regular on-demand subscription.

title: Jade Avedisian Returns to USAC Midget Racing Out West
text: After an injury sidelined her following a strong 2024 BC39 performance, Jade Avedisian returns to USAC NOS Energy Drink National Midget competition for select Golden State Invasion events this month. Jade Avedisian is back. The California driver, who put together a memorable run…
body: After an injury sidelined her following a strong 2024 BC39 performance, Jade Avedisian returns to USAC NOS Energy Drink National Midget competition for select Golden State Invasion events this month. Jade Avedisian is back. The California driver, who put together a memorable run at the 2024 BC39 at The Dirt Track at Indianapolis Motor Speedway before an injury forced her to step away from dirt midget racing, will return for select events on the USAC NOS Energy Drink National Midget Golden State Invasion. Avedisian will drive the Chad Boat Industries No. 89 at Plaza Park Raceway on November 18 (rescheduled for Monday, Nov. 23, according to USAC Media, Nov. 17 ; read the update ), Kevin Harvick's Kern Raceway (Bakersfield) on November 24, and Ventura Raceway on November 28 for the Turkey Night Grand Prix. All events will stream live on FloRacing. Her last USAC dirt midget start came at the BC39, where she came close to making history before the injury. She announced later in November 2024 that she needed time to heal properly. Now, nearly two years later, she's ready to get back behind the wheel out west.

title: Spencer Bayston Returning to Stenhouse Jr./Marshall Racing for 2027 World of Outlaws Season
text: Bayston confirmed during the World Finals that he will drive the NOS Energy Drink No. 17 again in 2027. He and crew chief Kyle Pruitt are looking to improve after what he called “a rebuilding year.” Spencer Bayston will return to Stenhouse Jr./Marshall Racing’s NOS Energy Drink…
body: Bayston confirmed during the World Finals that he will drive the NOS Energy Drink No. 17 again in 2027. He and crew chief Kyle Pruitt are looking to improve after what he called “a rebuilding year.” Spencer Bayston will return to Stenhouse Jr./Marshall Racing’s NOS Energy Drink No. 17 for the 2027 World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series season. Bayston confirmed the plan to Jacob Seelman of SWN on Friday, Nov. 6, during the World Finals at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. According to Seelman, Bayston said he and crew chief Kyle Pruitt have a lot they want to improve on to get the team past what he called “a rebuilding year.” The 2026 season was Bayston’s first with the team owned by Ricky Stenhouse Jr. and Richard and Jennifer Marshall, which hired him to replace Sheldon Haudenschild with Pruitt, formerly of Shark Racing, as crew chief. The pairing won the season opener on Feb. 4 at Volusia Speedway Park, where Bayston started 10th and passed Anthony Macri for the lead on lap 16. World of Outlaws statistics credit Bayston with one win, 15 top-five finishes and 36 top-10s in 68 feature starts in 2026. He finished 10th, 22nd and 12th in the three World Finals features. Bayston, of Lebanon, Ind., was the 2022 Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year with CJB Motorsports and has six career World of Outlaws wins. Sunday night at the World of Outlaws Awards Celebration in Charlotte, SJMR crew member Ace Pruitt, Kyle Pruitt’s son, was named the series’ Jason Johnson Sportsman of the Year . The 2027 World of Outlaws season begins Feb. 10-13 at Volusia Speedway Park’s Federated Auto Parts DIRTcar Nationals.

title: Brady Bacon to Run Full-Time High Limit Schedule With Vermeer Motorsports in 2027
text: Team owner Tony Vermeer named Bacon the full-time driver of the No. 55 on Oct. 22 after Bacon ran the final 10 races of 2026 in the car. It will be his first full-time national tour in a winged 410 sprint car. Brady Bacon will drive the Vermeer Motorsports No. 55 for the full…
body: Team owner Tony Vermeer named Bacon the full-time driver of the No. 55 on Oct. 22 after Bacon ran the final 10 races of 2026 in the car. It will be his first full-time national tour in a winged 410 sprint car. Brady Bacon will drive the Vermeer Motorsports No. 55 for the full Interstate Batteries High Limit Racing schedule in 2027, team owner Tony Vermeer announced on Oct. 22. Bacon drove the car in the final 10 races of the 2026 season. The 2027 season will be his first full-time national tour in a winged 410 sprint car, according to the announcement, which was published by SPEED SPORT and DirtRacing.com. “After a lengthy meeting, we’ve decided to name Brady Bacon as our driver for 2027. It’s pretty clear that he has the same mentality, the same passion, the same focus, and the same drive as Tye [Wolfgang] and myself…a ‘whatever it takes’ attitude,” Vermeer said. Crew chief Tye Wolfgang said Bacon’s “experience and accomplishments speak for themselves.” Bacon, 36, of Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, has won four USAC AMSOIL National Sprint Car championships and 64 series features, both second all-time in USAC history, according to the announcement. He raced the ASCS National Tour full time from 2010 to 2012 and won 12 times in that span, and he has two World of Outlaws wins. His busiest national touring season in a winged 410 was 2025, when he ran 17 of 48 High Limit events, which leaves him eligible for the 2027 Rayce Rudeen Foundation Rookie of the Year award. During the 10-race trial, Bacon and the No. 55 earned a podium finish at Lakeside Speedway and a top-five at Eldora Speedway, according to the announcement. Racing News reported that Bacon ran 13 High Limit events in 2026 with four top-five finishes, and FloRacing reported eight top-10s in those 13 starts. “Our goal is to build on that, win races, and ultimately, contend for a championship,” Bacon said. He also thanked CD Racing and TKH Motorsports for allowing him to pursue the full-time seat.

body: Danner leaves the No. 39 after the 2026 USAC season and is a free agent for 2027. As of now, Danner is a free agent heading into 2027.

title: Broedy Graham Wins 2026 USAC Western States Midget Championship
text: Graham finished fourth in the Ventura finale and won his first series title by 31 points after Drake Cardey spun with two laps left. He also won the Billy’s Tequila Cup. Broedy Graham of Bakersfield, California, is the 2026 USAC Avanti Windows & Doors Western States Midget…
body: Graham finished fourth in the Ventura finale and won his first series title by 31 points after Drake Cardey spun with two laps left. He also won the Billy’s Tequila Cup. Broedy Graham of Bakersfield, California, is the 2026 USAC Avanti Windows & Doors Western States Midget champion. The 18-year-old clinched the title with a fourth-place finish in the Nov. 7 season finale at Ventura Raceway, and his BGR Racing No. 66 team won the entrant title. Graham was running sixth with two laps to go while points leader Drake Cardey ran second. Cardey was caught in a four-car tangle at the bottom of Turn 2 and spun to a stop in the infield. He finished 15th, and Graham won the championship 863-832. Graham had taken the points lead from Cardey with one race left and held a six-point edge through an eight-week break before the finale. Graham led the series with 10 top-five finishes, four fast qualifying times and five heat race wins in 12 starts, and he tied Cardey for the most top-10 finishes with 11. His first two series wins came in back-to-back weeks, in June at Merced Speedway and on July 4 at Santa Maria Speedway. He is the third Bakersfield driver in four seasons to win the title, after Brody Fuson in 2023 and Cade Lewis in 2024. Graham also won the Billy’s Tequila Cup, a points title for the three Western States Midget races at Ventura, by one point over Jett Yantis. Cardey, who won at Imperial Valley in March and Santa Maria in June for Tom Dunkel Racing, was named Rookie of the Year. Yantis led the series with five wins, and C.J. Sarna was named Most Improved Driver after finishing third in points. Graham raced the season while playing defensive end as a senior on the Liberty High School football team. His younger brother, Blayden Graham, plans to join him in a two-car USAC Western States Midget effort in 2027.

title: Buddy Kofoid Returns as Defending Champion for $12,500-to-Win Jason Leffler Memorial at Bakersfield
text: The 12th Jason Leffler Memorial is Tuesday, Nov. 24, at Bakersfield Speedway at Kevin Harvick’s Kern Raceway. The 30-lap USAC National Midget feature pays $12,500 to win. Buddy Kofoid will return as the defending champion when the USAC NOS Energy Drink Midget National…
body: The 12th Jason Leffler Memorial is Tuesday, Nov. 24, at Bakersfield Speedway at Kevin Harvick’s Kern Raceway. The 30-lap USAC National Midget feature pays $12,500 to win. Buddy Kofoid will return as the defending champion when the USAC NOS Energy Drink Midget National Championship races the 12th Jason Leffler Memorial on Tuesday, Nov. 24, at Bakersfield Speedway at Kevin Harvick’s Kern Raceway, according to a USAC preview by Steven Blakesley. The 30-lap feature on the 1/3-mile dirt oval will pay $12,500 to win, USAC said. Kofoid, of Penngrove, California, won last year’s race at Bakersfield, the first time the memorial was held in California, and also won USAC’s most recent National Midget feature on Saturday at Merced Speedway. The event honors Jason Leffler of Long Beach, California, a three-time USAC National Midget champion in 1997, 1998 and 1999 and the 1998 USAC Silver Crown champion, USAC said. Among Leffler’s 19 career USAC National Midget feature wins are the 1997 Belleville Nationals, the 1997 Hut 100, the 1999 Copper World Classic, the 2002 Night Before the 500, and the 1999 and 2005 Turkey Night Grand Prix. He is an inductee of the National Midget Auto Racing Hall of Fame and the USAC Hall of Fame. USAC said the 2026 entry list includes Kyle Larson, whom the preview identified as a newly crowned three-time NASCAR Cup Series champion, and Corey Day of Clovis, California. Jade Avedisian, also of Clovis, will compete after returning to midget racing for the Golden State Invasion, according to USAC. Zach Daum, the 2013 winner, and Kofoid are the two past Jason Leffler Memorial champions listed on the preview. Other drivers named by USAC include series point leader Jacob Denney; national champions Justin Grant, Cannon McIntosh and Daison Pursley; National Midget winners Kale Drake, Kevin Thomas Jr., Hayden Reinbold, Jakeb Boxell and Gavin Miller; five-time 2026 USAC Western States Midget feature winner Jett Yantis; and 2026 USAC Western States Midget champion Broedy Graham. USAC event information lists pits opening at 2 p.m. Pacific, front gates at 4 p.m., a drivers meeting at 4:30 p.m. and cars on track at 5 p.m. IMCA SportMods are also on the card. The official purse pays $3,500 for second and $1,500 for third.

title: Buddy Kofoid Wins Chase Johnson Classic USAC Midget Feature at Merced
text: Kofoid started sixth and passed CB Industries teammate Justin Grant with four laps left after Grant’s car got a flat right front tire. It was Kofoid’s first series start for CBI. Buddy Kofoid won the 30-lap Chase Johnson Classic USAC NOS Energy Drink Midget National Championship…
body: Kofoid started sixth and passed CB Industries teammate Justin Grant with four laps left after Grant’s car got a flat right front tire. It was Kofoid’s first series start for CBI. Buddy Kofoid won the 30-lap Chase Johnson Classic USAC NOS Energy Drink Midget National Championship feature at Merced Speedway in Merced, California, on Saturday, Nov. 21, according to USAC. He started sixth and took the lead with four laps left. The race ran without a caution in 6:26.895 on the quarter-mile dirt oval, and Kofoid won by 0.717 seconds. USAC said it was Kofoid’s first series start for the CB Industries team. His first 25 series wins came with Keith Kunz/Curb-Agajanian Motorsports between 2020 and 2025. Kofoid’s CBI teammate Justin Grant led laps 2 through 26, according to the official lap leaders. USAC said Grant’s car bounced through turns one and two on lap 27 and landed with a flat right front tire. Kofoid passed him on the inside off turn two, and Grant fell to seventh. Jett Yantis started 10th and finished second, the best career USAC National Midget result for both Yantis and Beilman Motorsports, USAC said. Daison Pursley was third, Tanner Carrick fourth and polesitter Kale Drake, who led the first lap, fifth. Jacob Denney, Grant, Gavin Miller, Broedy Graham and Jakeb Boxell completed the top 10 in the 25-car field. Kofoid also set fast time at 11.997 seconds. According to USAC, he then won a wheelchair race among six drivers that set the lineup for the six-lap Chase for Cash Dash, and he won the dash in a track-record 1:13.227. USAC said the feature paid $5,000 to win. It was his 26th career USAC National Midget feature win, which moved him alone into 18th on the series’ all-time win list, and it made him Merced Speedway’s first three-time USAC National Midget feature winner. “But I’m glad to still be in position to take advantage of that and get a win during my first night out with Chad (Boat) and CBI,” Kofoid said, according to USAC. Denney leads the USAC National Midget standings with 1,191 points, ahead of Kevin Thomas Jr. with 1,086 and Grant with 1,067, according to USAC. The series is next scheduled to race Monday, Nov. 23, at Plaza Park Raceway in Visalia, California.

title: Buddy Kofoid Wins World of Outlaws Short Track Nationals at Texarkana
text: Kofoid passed Cole Macedo on a late restart for his 17th win of the season. Michael “Buddy” Kofoid won the 39th World of Outlaws Short Track Nationals on Saturday, Oct. 24, at Texarkana 67 Speedway in Texarkana, Ark. The 40-lap 410 feature paid $25,000 to win. On a restart with…
body: Kofoid passed Cole Macedo on a late restart for his 17th win of the season. Michael “Buddy” Kofoid won the 39th World of Outlaws Short Track Nationals on Saturday, Oct. 24, at Texarkana 67 Speedway in Texarkana, Ark. The 40-lap 410 feature paid $25,000 to win. On a restart with six laps to go, Kofoid ripped the cushion and completed a slide job past Cole Macedo in Turn 1 to take the lead. The win was Kofoid’s 17th of 2026 in the Roth Motorsports No. 83, breaking the Roth Motorsports single-season World of Outlaws win record of 16 set by Danny Lasoski in 1999. Top 5: 1. body: The Danish driver will race the No. 98 Agajanian Special for Johnny Cofer and Dan Esslinger in the 85th Turkey Night Grand Prix, the USAC National Midget season finale, on Nov. 28 at Ventura Raceway. NTT IndyCar Series race winner Christian Rasmussen will make his USAC NOS Energy Drink National Midget debut in the 85th ARP Turkey Night Grand Prix on Saturday, Nov. 28, at Ventura Raceway in Ventura, California. The 26-year-old from Copenhagen, Denmark, drives the No. 21 Chevrolet for Ed Carpenter Racing in IndyCar, where he won for the first time at the Milwaukee Mile on Aug. 24, 2025. Rasmussen will drive the No. 98, a Spike short-arm chassis with an SR-11 engine fielded by car owner Johnny Cofer. With support from the Agajanian family, the car will carry a paint scheme based on the 1952 Agajanian Special that Troy Ruttman drove to victory in the Indianapolis 500. The entry reunites Cofer and Dan Esslinger, who won the 1994 USAC Western States Midget championship together with Cofer driving and Esslinger as owner. Cofer's daughter, Maria Cofer, has raced the same car. "I'm excited to try something that is completely out of my wheelhouse," Rasmussen said. "But most of all, I'm excited to get to work with Johnny Cofer and Dan Esslinger." Esslinger described it as a one-race deal for now. Rasmussen won the USF2000 title in 2020, the Indy Pro 2000 title in 2021 and the INDY NXT title in 2023. He also won the LMP2 class at the 2024 Rolex 24 at Daytona. Practice for Turkey Night is Friday, Nov. 27. Qualifying, heat races and the 98-lap main event are Saturday, Nov. 28, and the race will stream on FloRacing.

title: Nov 4: Cale Coons Named 2026 USAC National Sprint Car Rookie of the Year
text: Cale Coons of Greencastle, Indiana, earned the 2026 USAC AMSOIL Sprint Car National Championship Max Papis Innovations Rookie of the Year after a full-time debut that included his first series feature win. Coons, the 17-year-old son of USAC Triple Crown champion Jerry Coons Jr.,…
body: Cale Coons of Greencastle, Indiana, earned the 2026 USAC AMSOIL Sprint Car National Championship Max Papis Innovations Rookie of the Year after a full-time debut that included his first series feature win. Coons, the 17-year-old son of USAC Triple Crown champion Jerry Coons Jr., finished 11th in the national points in the Dooling Autosports-Curb-Agajanian No. 63. He scored one feature win, four top-fives, 23 top-10s, 32 laps led and a series-leading 16 heat victories. He is the first son of a past USAC National Sprint Car champion to win the series Rookie of the Year award, according to a USAC media release carried by FloRacing. His breakthrough came at Kokomo Speedway’s Sprint Car Smackdown. After finishing third on opening night, Coons led 29 of 30 laps the following night for his first USAC National Sprint Car win. Thomas Meseraull briefly took the lead after Coons’ early run up front; Coons slid back by one lap later and held on. He is the first USAC National Sprint Car Rookie of the Year to also win a feature in the same season since Emerson Axsom in 2022. Coons and Jerry Coons Jr. became the 10th father-son duo to each win a USAC National Sprint Car main event as drivers. Coons contested all 48 USAC National Sprint Car events in 2026, missing the feature transfer only twice. One of those nights, at Bloomington during Indiana Sprint Week, he used a provisional, started 25th and finished seventh — a plus-18 that ranked as the second-biggest feature advance of the season. He also finished second in the Bomb City 40 at Route 66 Motor Speedway in Amarillo, Texas, and collected three Rod End Supply Hard Charger awards earlier in the year.

title: Kyle Cummins Seeking Ownership Partners for 2027 USAC Return
text: The two-time and defending USAC AMSOIL National Sprint Car champion is pursuing ownership and partnership options to keep the championship-winning team together after Petty Performance Racing ends its national program. Kyle Cummins is pursuing ownership and partnership…
body: The two-time and defending USAC AMSOIL National Sprint Car champion is pursuing ownership and partnership options to keep the championship-winning team together after Petty Performance Racing ends its national program. Kyle Cummins is pursuing ownership and partnership opportunities to keep his championship-winning national sprint car team intact and return to the USAC AMSOIL Sprint Car National Tour in 2027, according to a Nov. 5, 2026 Kyle Cummins Racing update. The move follows Petty Performance Racing’s decision to conclude its involvement in the national sprint car program after back-to-back titles with Cummins. Jerry Petty and his wife, Bev, are stepping away from the national program to devote more time to family. In a post-season interview with USAC Racing, Petty said the future of the USAC National team would be up to Cummins, and that Petty Performance Racing would not continue the national program into 2027. USAC’s 2026 season review similarly reported that the Petty Performance Racing national team was shutting down and would not continue next year. Petty has entrusted Cummins with guiding the team’s next chapter. Cummins, of Princeton, Indiana, won the 2025 and 2026 USAC AMSOIL National Sprint Car titles in the Petty Performance Racing No. 3p. In 2026 he led the series with 11 wins, 351 laps led, 35 top-fives and 45 top-10s in 48 feature starts, according to USAC. Across the two-year run with Petty Performance Racing, Cummins recorded 21 wins, 73 top-fives and 89 top-10s in 97 starts. The Nov. 5 update outlines a plan to preserve the winning formula: retain core crew members Cameron LaRose, Kasey DeRenzy and Zach Fields, with Cummins continuing as the driver. Those three were identified by USAC as core team members during the 2026 championship season. Possible paths include a complete team acquisition, a new ownership structure, strategic investment or long-term corporate sponsorship; terms were described as open. No contact information is published here because a public copy of the full release with inquiry details could not be independently located for verification.

title: Cy Fairchild, Michigan Racer and USAC Sprint Car Winner, Dies at 91
text: The Michigan driver won his first feature at 15, co-drove to the 1967 Little 500 win and scored two USAC sprint car victories at New Bremen, Ohio. Cy Fairchild, a USAC sprint car feature winner from Michigan, died on Nov. 15, 2026, at the age of 91, USAC reported. Fairchild,…
body: The Michigan driver won his first feature at 15, co-drove to the 1967 Little 500 win and scored two USAC sprint car victories at New Bremen, Ohio. Cy Fairchild, a USAC sprint car feature winner from Michigan, died on Nov. 15, 2026, at the age of 91, USAC reported. Fairchild, whose full name was Cyrus LaGrande Fairchild Jr., competed from 1952 through about 1979 and was reported to have won more than 800 feature races during his career, according to the USAC obituary by Stan Kalwasinski. Fairchild, a boxer in his younger days, won his first main event in 1952 in a Ford coupe at Michigan’s Dixie Motor Speedway at 15 years of age, USAC said. He was tough to beat at Michigan tracks including Dixie, Zilwaukee, Auburn, Owosso and Cadillac before moving to sprint cars with the International Motor Contest Association and USAC. He co-drove with Ohio’s Darl Harrison to victory in the 1967 IMCA-sanctioned Little 500 at Sun Valley Speedway in Anderson, Indiana, taking over in relief at the 384-lap mark and finishing with a three-lap lead in the Loren Weyant-Tom Schemmer, Chevy-powered No. 91. Fairchild began racing with USAC in 1968 and finished 11th in that year’s final sprint car standings, according to USAC. He won a non-points USAC race in the second leg of the “triple 33s” at Ohio’s Dayton Speedway in September 1968 in the Stahl Brothers No. 36. In 1969 he finished sixth in USAC points and won his first USAC feature at New Bremen Speedway in Ohio that April in the Stahl Brothers car. He was badly injured in a USAC sprint car race at New Bremen in April 1970 and returned to score his second and final USAC win there on Oct. 24, 1971, driving a converted Indianapolis 500 roadster owned by Ben Leyba. Fairchild entered the 1969 Indianapolis 500 but wrecked his Lotus in practice and did not qualify, and he attempted to qualify for NASCAR’s Daytona 500 in 1966 but did not make the race, USAC said. A cattle rancher, he was for a time the promoter at Tri-City Speedway in Auburn, Michigan. He was inducted into the Michigan Motorsports Hall of Fame in 1988.

title: Steven Drevicki Wins Sixth USAC East Coast Sprint Car Title
text: The Reading, Pennsylvania driver claimed his record-extending sixth USAC East Coast Sprint Cars Presented by Baer Den Farms championship, 28 points ahead of Christian Bruno. Steven Drevicki of Reading, Pennsylvania won his record-extending sixth career USAC East Coast Sprint…
body: The Reading, Pennsylvania driver claimed his record-extending sixth USAC East Coast Sprint Cars Presented by Baer Den Farms championship, 28 points ahead of Christian Bruno. Steven Drevicki of Reading, Pennsylvania won his record-extending sixth career USAC East Coast Sprint Cars Presented by Baer Den Farms championship in 2026. The 35-year-old closed out the closest points race in series history, finishing 28 points ahead of Christian Bruno of Deptford, New Jersey, 847-819. The previous closest title fight was 44 points in the series’ inaugural 2018 season, also won by Drevicki. All six of Drevicki’s titles have come in his own No. 19. He won the first three series championships in 2018, 2019 and 2020, then completed a second three-peat in 2024, 2025 and 2026. He recorded two feature victories, both at Bridgeport Motorsports Park in New Jersey, a series-high 11 top-five finishes, and top-10 results in all 12 of his feature starts. After chasing the point lead for much of the season, he took over the top spot from Bruno with three races remaining and closed with a fourth, a win and a sixth in his final three starts. Drevicki credited a midseason stretch of top-five finishes in Pennsylvania and New Jersey, including a wire-to-wire win at Bridgeport in August in which he led all 25 laps. In a September return to Bridgeport, he slid J.R. Fulper for the lead in a three-car battle with two laps remaining; Fulper’s car then began to stumble without fuel. “It’s wild to think about six,” Drevicki said. “I don’t know that it’s even sunk in.” Five drivers won USAC East Coast features in 2026: Bruno, Briggs Danner, Drevicki, Kenny Miller III and Chelby Hinton. Bruno led the series with five victories — Big Diamond Speedway in May, a three-race sweep at Selinsgrove Speedway, and Port Royal Speedway in September — and also led the tour in laps led (69) and heat-race wins (7). He finished second in the standings for the second time in the last three years. Miller was third, Kyle Spence fourth and Joe Kata fifth, both Spence and Kata posting their best career series points finishes. Olivia Thayer was named Rookie of the Year. Four drivers started all 12 features: Bruno, Drevicki, Kata and Miller.

title: Edwards Wins 2024 USAC Western States Midget Finale at Kern; Cade Lewis Clinches Title
text: Drake Edwards passed Cade Lewis just before the midpoint of the 30-lap feature at Kevin Harvick’s Kern Raceway on Oct. 5, 2024. Lewis finished third and won the series championship by 11 points. Drake Edwards of Surprise, Arizona won the Avanti Windows & Doors USAC Western…
body: Drake Edwards passed Cade Lewis just before the midpoint of the 30-lap feature at Kevin Harvick’s Kern Raceway on Oct. 5, 2024. Lewis finished third and won the series championship by 11 points. Drake Edwards of Surprise, Arizona won the Avanti Windows & Doors USAC Western States Midget season finale on Oct. 5, 2024 at The Dirt Track at Kevin Harvick’s Kern Raceway in Bakersfield, California. Edwards passed Cade Lewis just before the midpoint of the 30-lap feature for his second series victory of the season and also earned Rookie of the Year honors with a runner-up finish in the final points. Ben Worth of Coalinga, California led the first seven laps from the outside of the front row before Edwards slid in front in turn two on lap eight. Contact between those two allowed Lewis to drive from third to first. Lewis led laps eight and nine on the bottom before Edwards used the high side to lead lap 10. Sparks and a ball of flame then came from the back of Edwards’ car as he got on the brakes in turns one and two, and Lewis led laps 11 and 12. Edwards drove around the outside of Lewis off turn two to retake the lead for good on lap 13. Jett Yantis of Bakersfield, the night’s fast qualifier, passed Lewis for second and challenged Edwards on the final lap, but a slide-job attempt entering turn three was stifled when ninth-place Kyle Hawse occupied the low line. Edwards held on for the win. Yantis finished second, Lewis third, Brandt Twitty fourth and Dane Culver fifth. Worth, who led the opening seven laps, retired after an incident in turns one and two. Lewis, of Bakersfield, won the series driving championship by 11 points over Edwards, 622-611, the first title of his career. The result also gave car owner Dean Alexander of New Zealand his first series entrant championship. Edwards started fourth in the Petty Performance Racing No. 3p and also won the first heat.

body: Gile led the final 11 laps at Casa Grande, Ariz., on Saturday, Nov. 21, and Petty Performance Racing took the top three spots. Runner-up R.J. Johnson clinched the series title. Elijah Gile won the 25-lap USAC Avanti Windows & Doors Southwest Sprint Car feature at Central Arizona Raceway in Casa Grande, Arizona, on Saturday, Nov. 21, according to USAC. The win completed his sweep of both nights of the second Dennis Matousek Memorial Race. Gile’s Petty Performance Racing teammate R.J. Johnson finished second and clinched his sixth career USAC Southwest Sprint Car championship, USAC said. Gile started third. J.J. Yeley led the first lap, and Johnson led laps 2 through 9. Gile led lap 10, Johnson led laps 11 through 14, and Gile led laps 15 through 25, according to the official lap leaders. USAC said Gile passed Johnson for the lead in turn one on lap 15 and won by 7.898 seconds for his third career USAC Southwest Sprint Car win. Petty Performance Racing swept the top three, with Cameron La Rose in third. Stevie Sussex was fourth and Yeley fifth. Dayton Shelton, Connor Lundy, Koen Crawford, A.J. Hernandez and Bruce St. James completed the top 10 in the 22-car feature. Johnson also won the USAC Southwest title in 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2017, USAC said. According to USAC, he is the first driver to win the USAC CRA 410 and USAC Southwest 360 sprint car championships in the same season, a feat he shares with car owner Jerry Petty. Earlier this season, Johnson won his third straight USAC CRA Sprint Car title . Gile set fast time at 15.584 seconds among 23 qualifiers, USAC said. Yeley won the dash, and Sussex, Shelton and Johnson won the three eight-lap heat races. According to USAC, the race honors Gile’s great-grandfather Dennis Matousek, an Arizona Racing Association sprint car champion and Arizona Motorsports Hall of Fame inductee. Gile also won the inaugural edition in 2025, and he won Friday’s opening night .

title: Elijah Gile Wins USAC Southwest Sprint Car Feature at Central Arizona Raceway
text: Gile started ninth in the Petty Performance Racing No. 13p and passed polesitter J.J. Yeley with two laps to go on opening night of the Dennis Matousek Memorial at Casa Grande, Ariz., on Friday, Nov. 20. Elijah Gile won the 25-lap USAC Avanti Windows & Doors Southwest Sprint Car…
body: Gile started ninth in the Petty Performance Racing No. 13p and passed polesitter J.J. Yeley with two laps to go on opening night of the Dennis Matousek Memorial at Casa Grande, Ariz., on Friday, Nov. 20. Elijah Gile won the 25-lap USAC Avanti Windows & Doors Southwest Sprint Car feature at Central Arizona Raceway in Casa Grande, Arizona, on Friday, Nov. 20, the opening night of the Dennis Matousek Memorial Race, according to USAC. It was the Phoenix driver’s second career series win, after his first in August at Deuce of Clubs Thunder Raceway in Show Low, Arizona. USAC said Matousek, an Arizona Racing Association sprint car champion and Arizona Motorsports Hall of Fame inductee who died in January 2025, was Gile’s great-grandfather, and that Gile also won the inaugural edition of the race in 2025. Gile started ninth in the Petty Performance Racing No. 13p. Yeley started on the pole and led laps 1 through 23 before Gile took the lead and led the final two laps, according to the official lap leaders. Yeley finished second, 1.232 seconds behind. A.J. Hernandez was third, Koen Crawford fourth and Chaz Baca fifth. R.J. Johnson, Dayton Shelton, Charles Davis Jr., Cameron La Rose and Connor Lundy completed the top 10 in the 21-car feature. Johnson set fast time at 16.063 seconds among 23 qualifiers, USAC said. Baca, Shelton and Gile won the three eight-lap heat races. In the 360 winged sprint car feature on the same program, D.J. Netto of Hanford, California, was the winner, according to Central Arizona Raceway’s event results. The Dennis Matousek Memorial concludes Saturday, Nov. 21, at Central Arizona Raceway, according to USAC.

title: Mitch Fabish Wins Third Straight Baypark Midget Feature
text: Te Awamutu’s Mitch Fabish extended his unbeaten start to the New Zealand speedway season with a third consecutive Midget Car feature win, taking the Easysteel Bill Buckley Classic at Baypark Speedway by 0.608 seconds over Alec Insley. Mitch Fabish continues to dominate early in…
body: Te Awamutu’s Mitch Fabish extended his unbeaten start to the New Zealand speedway season with a third consecutive Midget Car feature win, taking the Easysteel Bill Buckley Classic at Baypark Speedway by 0.608 seconds over Alec Insley. Mitch Fabish continues to dominate early in the 2026-27 New Zealand midget season. On Sunday night at Baypark Speedway, he held off Auckland teenager Alec Insley throughout a caution-free 25-lap feature to win the Easysteel Bill Buckley Classic. The victory follows wins at Baypark’s Labour Weekend season opener and the Rosetown 40-lapper at Kihikihi the previous weekend. Fabish’s early form has him firmly in the conversation as the New Zealand Midget Championship approaches. In the Sprint Car feature the same night, former New Zealand champion Jonathan Allard led from start to finish for his second win of the season.

title: Daison Pursley Won the Last Hangtown 100 and Is Already a USAC Midget Champion at 22
text: The Locust Grove, Okla., driver won the most recent Hangtown 100, the opener of USAC’s California midget swing, five years after a crash that left him paralyzed from the neck down. The USAC NOS Energy Drink National Midgets finish the 2026 season with seven races in California,…
body: The Locust Grove, Okla., driver won the most recent Hangtown 100, the opener of USAC’s California midget swing, five years after a crash that left him paralyzed from the neck down. The USAC NOS Energy Drink National Midgets finish the 2026 season with seven races in California, the Golden State Invasion, starting with the Hangtown 100 at Placerville Speedway on Nov. 13-14. The swing continues at Plaza Park Raceway in Visalia on Nov. 18 (rescheduled for Monday, Nov. 23, according to USAC Media, Nov. 17 ; read the update ), the track’s first date on the series schedule, then the Chase Johnson Classic at Merced Speedway on Nov. 20-21, the Jason Leffler Memorial at Bakersfield Speedway at Kevin Harvick’s Kern Raceway on Nov. 24 and the 85th Turkey Night Grand Prix at Ventura Raceway on Nov. 28, according to USAC’s schedule . The most recent Hangtown 100, in 2025, was won by Daison Pursley of Locust Grove, Okla., who turned 22 on Oct. 20. The 2024 edition was canceled for rain and cold. Pursley started fourth in a 25-car field on Nov. 15, 2025, and stayed in the top four for all 100 laps. On lap 96 he was second and tried to pass leader Kyle Larson in turn one; Pursley’s car appeared to clip the infield berm and slid into Larson’s, which flipped. Pursley finished 0.257 seconds ahead of Steven Snyder Jr. for $20,000, USAC reported . He apologized afterward and said he had not wanted to win that way. The win was one entry on a long USAC list. Pursley won the National Midget championship in 2024 with CB Industries and the Indiana Midget Week title the same year, and he was the 2023 National Sprint Car Rookie of the Year, the 2023 and 2024 National Passing Master champion and the 2017 National Micro Sprint champion, according to USAC’s driver page . That page, last updated on Jan. 1, 2026, credits him with 11 National Midget wins in 136 starts through 2025, seven of them in 2024. At the 2025 4-Crown Nationals at Eldora Speedway he won the National Sprint Car, National Midget and Silver Crown features in one night, joining Jack Hewitt, Larson and Logan Seavey as the fourth driver to do so. His career nearly ended at 17. A crash at Arizona Speedway in November 2021 broke his neck, and he was diagnosed as an incomplete quadriplegic. After surgery and rehabilitation at the Shepherd Center in Atlanta, he attended the 2022 Chili Bowl Nationals in Tulsa that January, returned to racing in August 2022 and was back in victory lane that September, according to KJRH and FloRacing . He finished second to Larson in the 2025 Chili Bowl Nationals and sixth in the 2026 A-feature. Pursley has also moved into winged sprint cars. He won at Lernerville Speedway on Sept. 13, 2025, and was named the High Limit Racing Rookie of the Year driving for Buch Motorsports. In October 2025 Kasey Kahne Racing hired him as its full-time driver of the No. 9 for 2026, after Brad Sweet stepped away from full-time touring, FloRacing reported , and Placerville Speedway’s preview for this week’s race calls him a High Limit regular. On Sept. 26, 2026, he led all 50 laps in the USAC Silver Crown feature at the 4-Crown Nationals, the debut of the Spire Motorsports/CB Industries Silver Crown team, for his fifth career 4-Crown win as a driver, Speed Sport reported .

title: From Speedcar Champion to Two-Time WA Sprintcar Champion: Dayne Kingshott’s Rise With Krikke Motorsport
text: The Bunbury driver won his second Western Australian Sprintcar Championship on Nov. 7, 2026, at his team’s home track, four seasons after his first and nearly eight years after winning the Australian Speedcar Championship. Dayne Kingshott won the Western Australian Sprintcar…
body: The Bunbury driver won his second Western Australian Sprintcar Championship on Nov. 7, 2026, at his team’s home track, four seasons after his first and nearly eight years after winning the Australian Speedcar Championship. Dayne Kingshott won the Western Australian Sprintcar Championship on Nov. 7, 2026, at Bunbury Speedway, leading every lap of the 35-lap feature after starting second, according to Auto Action . It was his second state title, Krikke Motorsport’s ninth and the team’s first win of the 2026-27 season. Callum Williamson finished second, Kaiden Manders third, Kris Coyle fourth and Daniel Harding fifth. The race was round three of the Maddington Toyota Sprintcar Series, and Speedway Illustrated News reported in July that it was the first time in some while the event had been run at the South West venue. Kingshott, who drives the WA No. 2 Mobil 1/Bunbury Toyota-backed Maxim, said the win meant more because it was the team’s first together at Bunbury, where many of its sponsors are local, the team said . His route to the title began in speedcars. The Bunbury resident won the Australian Speedcar Championship at Perth Motorplex on Feb. 9, 2019, ahead of Adam Clarke of New South Wales and American Jason McDougal. He moved to 410 Sprintcars with Krikke Motorsport for 2020-21, when pandemic travel restrictions kept Kerry Madsen from driving the team’s car, and finished second in the SEG Series standings that season, according to the team’s history page . He won his first 410 Sprintcar feature with the team in 2021-22, along with the Perth Motorplex Track Championship. His first state title came on Dec. 3, 2022, in the 61st running of the event at Perth Motorplex. Starting third, Kingshott took the lead from James Inglis with about six laps to go in a 35-lap feature that took more than an hour because of repeated stoppages, and finished ahead of Taylor Milling and Inglis. Krikke Motorsport called it the team’s eighth Western Australian title, following Ron Krikke in 1983-84 and 1984-85, John Krikke in 1988-89, Brooke Tatnell in 2013-14, Jamie Veal in 2017-18 and Madsen in 2018-19 and 2019-20. The state titles sit beside a run of consistent seasons. Kingshott won the Maddington Toyota Sprintcar Series in 2023-24 with 2,820 points, the first series championship for Krikke Motorsport, after finishing second, third and fourth in the previous three seasons. He repeated in 2024-25 with 3,222 points, 52 ahead of Williamson, and won a third series title in 2025-26 with six round wins. In November 2025 he became the first driver to win the King of Wings three years in a row, beating James McFadden by 0.010 seconds at Perth Motorplex. In December, at the 2025 High Limit International at Perth Motorplex, he finished second to Kyle Larson in the $110,000-to-win race. Among Western Australian champions, Kingshott now has two titles. Perth Motorplex credits Alf Barbagallo, known as “Mr. Sprintcar,” with six, and the Sprintcar World honour roll, which begins in 2009, lists Jason Kendrick (2011, 2014 and 2021) and Madsen (2010, 2018 and 2019) with three each. Kingshott sits seventh in the 2026-27 series standings, and Krikke Motorsport has said it is aiming for a fourth Maddington Toyota Sprintcar Series championship. The next round is the King of Wings at Perth Motorplex on Nov. 14, where Kingshott is the three-time defending winner.

title: Emerson Axsom Follows Chili Bowl Win With World of Outlaws Rookie of the Year Title
text: The Franklin, Ind., driver won the Golden Driller in January, took his first World of Outlaws feature in September and closed his first full-time season as the Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year. Emerson Axsom finished his first full-time World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint…
body: The Franklin, Ind., driver won the Golden Driller in January, took his first World of Outlaws feature in September and closed his first full-time season as the Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year. Emerson Axsom finished his first full-time World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series season as the Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year presented by Five Star Bodies, an award announced at the series’ awards celebration on Nov. 8 in Charlotte, N.C. ( our banquet report ). The year began with a win in the Chili Bowl Nationals, a crown jewel, and included his first series feature victory. World of Outlaws statistics credit Axsom and the Klaasmeyer/Petry Motorsports No. 27 with one win, 11 top-five finishes, 32 top 10s and 66 laps led, and the series’ points table lists him ninth with 8,946 points. Axsom won the 40th Chili Bowl Nationals on Jan. 17 in Tulsa, Okla., driving the No. 39A for Kevin Swindell’s team. Swindell, a four-time Chili Bowl winner as a driver, had messaged him on Instagram the previous summer to ask if he wanted the ride, NASCAR.com reported. Starting second in the 55-lap A-feature, Axsom passed pole-sitter Kyle Larson, the 2025 winner, on the fourth lap. On lap 16 Larson flipped after contact with the slowed car of C.J. Leary and was eliminated, and Axsom held the lead through challenges from Logan Seavey and Justin Grant. A late caution for Grant’s flip in turn three set up a green-white-checkered finish, and Axsom held off Kevin Thomas Jr., who had started 18th, to win. Hank Davis was third, Seavey fourth and Briggs Danner fifth, according to the official results. The win followed several seasons of moving between divisions. According to the World of Outlaws, Axsom ran the USAC National Midget Series in 2021 and USAC National Sprint Cars in 2022 and 2023, then committed fully to winged sprint cars in 2024 with Klaasmeyer/Petry Motorsports, winning that year at Lincoln Park Speedway and Knoxville Raceway. He was the Knoxville Nationals Rookie of the Year in 2024 and won his first All Star Circuit of Champions feature at Eldora Speedway in 2025. In July 2025 he filled in for two months in the KCP Racing No. 18 after Giovanni Scelzi and the team separated, then returned to the Klaasmeyer/Petry car. On Feb. 3, 2026, the series announced he would run the full World of Outlaws schedule in the No. 27 for car owners Dale Klaasmeyer and Scott Petry. His father, Joe Axsom, serves as crew chief. The season started slowly. Axsom had no top 10s in his first six races, then finished second at Tri-State Speedway in Haubstadt, Ind., on April 19, his best result of the year at that point. That finish moved him 28 points ahead of Ashton Torgerson in the rookie standings, the World of Outlaws reported. His first win came Sept. 6 at Huset’s Speedway in Brandon, S.D., in the L.G. Everist Huset’s Shootout finale. Starting second in the 40-lap feature, he traded the lead with Carson Macedo and held off David Gravel and Michael Kofoid on late restarts for a $25,000 payday. The series listed him as its 160th different feature winner, the fifth first-time winner of 2026 and the 21st different winner of the season. Axsom was strong through the second half. Before the World Finals, the World of Outlaws noted he had 19 top 10s in his previous 23 races. At The Dirt Track at Charlotte he won Thursday’s C-main to qualify for the feature, started 25th and finished 22nd. He was 12th on Friday and 18th on Saturday, qualifying for all three A-mains. Under the Five Star Bodies program announced by the World of Outlaws in February, the sprint car Rookie of the Year receives a new body and a $10,000 bonus. The 2027 World of Outlaws season opens Feb. 10-13 at Volusia Speedway Park in Barberville, Fla.

title: Jason Johnson’s 2016 Knoxville Nationals Upset Ended Donny Schatz's Reign by 0.168 Seconds
text: The Eunice, La., driver beat the nine-time champion in the Priority Aviation No. 41 to win a crown jewel and the $150,000 first prize at the 56th Nationals. On Aug. 13, 2016, Jason Johnson of Eunice, La., beat Donny Schatz by 0.168 seconds to win the 56th 5-Hour Energy Knoxville…
body: The Eunice, La., driver beat the nine-time champion in the Priority Aviation No. 41 to win a crown jewel and the $150,000 first prize at the 56th Nationals. On Aug. 13, 2016, Jason Johnson of Eunice, La., beat Donny Schatz by 0.168 seconds to win the 56th 5-Hour Energy Knoxville Nationals presented by Casey’s General Stores, a crown jewel, and the $150,000 first prize. The official World of Outlaws recap, titled “Cajun-Style Upset,” said the result denied Schatz a 10th Nationals win. Schatz, already a nine-time champion of the event, started fifth. Johnson started second in the Priority Aviation No. 41 Maxim. Shane Stewart finished third, pole-sitter Daryn Pittman was fourth and Kyle Larson was fifth after starting 21st. Larson was the hard charger. Johnson earned the outside front row after a runner-up finish on preliminary Night 2 made him the high-point driver of that session, the World of Outlaws reported. Kerry Madsen and Jamie Veal started third and fourth. Pittman led the first 10 laps of the 50-lap A-main. Official lap leaders show Johnson in front on lap 11, Pittman back in front on lap 12 and Schatz taking the lead on lap 13. Schatz still led when a mandatory caution came at halfway and through lap 26. On the second-half restart, Johnson used the cushion, took the lead on lap 27 and nearly climbed the wall on lap 34, according to the official recap. Schatz regained the lead on laps 44 and 45. The two traded slide jobs over the final segment, and the World of Outlaws said they made contact, before Johnson led laps 46 through 50. “I gave it my all,” Johnson said. “I wanted to win just as bad as Donny wanted to win.” Schatz said Johnson “did one hell of a job” and “earned it.” In victory lane Johnson said, “Parked it, BC,” a dedication T.J. Buffenbarger recorded for TJSlideways.com. Bryan Clauson had died on Aug. 7, 2016, of injuries from a crash the night before at the Belleville (Kan.) Nationals, Indianapolis Motor Speedway reported. The official World of Outlaws recap also quoted Johnson calling the win “a testament to friendship, to what life is all about, and to B.C.” The finish stood out against the series standings. After the race, unofficial World of Outlaws points listed Johnson seventh with two feature wins, 12 top-fives and 31 top-10s. Schatz led the championship with 16 wins. Buffenbarger called the Nationals victory an upset and wrote that Johnson had not won a World of Outlaws feature since March 23 at Placerville Speedway and that his best finish leading into the event was fifth on Aug. 5 at Federated Auto Parts Raceway at I-55 in Pevely, Mo. Johnson died of injuries from a crash on June 23, 2018, during the Jim Boyd Memorial at Beaver Dam Raceway in Wisconsin. He was 41. A World of Outlaws memorial later credited him with 12 series feature wins, five American Sprint Car Series championships and the 2016 Knoxville Nationals title, his only win in that crown jewel. The series still runs the Jason Johnson Classic in his memory. Carson Macedo won the 2026 edition on Oct. 23 at Texarkana 67 Speedway in the Jason Johnson Racing No. 41.

title: Kyle Larson Returns to Placerville With Four Hangtown 100 Wins and a Co-Promoter’s Stake
text: The Elk Grove, Calif., driver has four Hangtown 100 USAC National Midget feature wins at Placerville — the inaugural 100-lapper in 2019, a preliminary feature in 2021, and both nights in 2023 — and enters the Nov. 13-14, 2026 running as co-promoter, racing both a midget and a…
body: The Elk Grove, Calif., driver has four Hangtown 100 USAC National Midget feature wins at Placerville — the inaugural 100-lapper in 2019, a preliminary feature in 2021, and both nights in 2023 — and enters the Nov. 13-14, 2026 running as co-promoter, racing both a midget and a 360 sprint car. Kyle Larson goes into the Hangtown 100 at Placerville Speedway on Nov. 13-14, 2026, entered in both the USAC NOS Energy Drink National Midgets and winged 360 sprint cars on each day, FloRacing reported . He arrives five days after clinching his third NASCAR Cup Series championship at Homestead-Miami Speedway on Nov. 8, according to NASCAR.com and NBC Sports . The Hangtown 100 is the only 100-lap USAC National Midget main event on the 2026 schedule and opens the series’ seven-race Golden State Invasion in California, USAC said . Larson has four Hangtown 100 USAC National Midget feature wins at Placerville Speedway, the official total on USAC’s 2025 event preview : Nov. 20, 2019; Nov. 19, 2021; and both nights in 2023, Nov. 17 and Nov. 19. The race debuted in 2019 under original promoter Matt Wood. On Nov. 20, 2019, Larson started 10th in a 28-car field, took the lead on lap 35 and led the final 66 laps, finishing 8.152 seconds ahead of Christopher Bell. He earned $20,000 for the 100-lap feature and a $12,000 bonus as the event’s overall points champion, a $32,000 total that USAC described as the richest event in the history of its National and Western States Midget divisions. In 2021 he won the Nov. 19 preliminary feature, and Justin Grant won the 100-lap finale the next night. Buddy Kofoid won the 100-lapper in 2022. The 2024 edition was canceled because of rain and cold. In 2023 he swept both features. The Friday opener was a 30-lap race that he led from lap 6 and finished in 6 minutes, 14.69 seconds without a caution. On Sunday, Nov. 19, he started 16th after the random draw gave the points leader that spot, passed Logan Seavey for the lead on lap 93 and won by 0.881 seconds. USAC reported that he became the first two-time winner of the 100-lapper and the first driver to win a second overall Hangtown 100 points championship, for a $25,500 weekend. The Sunday win was his 27th in the USAC National Midget Series, tying Gary Bettenhausen and Tony Stewart for 15th on the all-time list. Larson became co-promoter in October 2025, when Russell Motorsports announced the partnership. That year’s Friday opener was washed out by nearly 3.5 inches of rain, leaving one program on Saturday, Nov. 15. Larson set fast time, started 11th, took the lead on lap 44 and led a race-high 52 laps. On lap 96, Daison Pursley, who had moved into second, tried to pass for the lead in turn one, and contact sent Larson’s car flipping. Larson finished 15th and Pursley won, USAC reported . Pursley apologized afterward and said he had not wanted to win that way, and Larson called it a bummer but said he understood the move. Placerville has been part of Larson’s career since his teens. He made his first sprint car start at the track in 2007 and won there that August at age 15, becoming the youngest feature winner in the speedway’s history at the time, according to a contemporary Civil War Series report. He also clinched the 2010 Golden State KWS-NARC Series championship there. This year the Hangtown 100 adds winged 360 sprint cars on both days for the first time as a companion class, with $2,000 to win each night, and racing starts at 2 p.m. PT with gates opening at 1 p.m., the track said .

title: David Gravel Clinches Third Straight World of Outlaws Championship
text: David Gravel finished sixth in Thursday’s World Finals feature at The Dirt Track at Charlotte to clinch his third consecutive World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series title. David Gravel clinched his third consecutive World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car…
body: David Gravel finished sixth in Thursday’s World Finals feature at The Dirt Track at Charlotte to clinch his third consecutive World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series title. David Gravel clinched his third consecutive World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series championship Thursday night at the Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals at The Dirt Track at Charlotte in Concord, N.C. Gravel, driving the Big Game Motorsports No. 2, started fifth and finished sixth in the 25-lap feature won by Rico Abreu. That finish locked up the title. Gravel is only the fourth driver in series history to win three straight World of Outlaws championships, joining Steve Kinser, Donny Schatz and Brad Sweet. The title is the third of his career, which ties him with Sammy Swindell for the fourth-most championships in series history. Gravel and Big Game Motorsports won their first title together in 2024 and repeated in 2025. Gravel entered the World Finals with a 124-point lead over Michael “Buddy” Kofoid, according to official World of Outlaws standings. Before Thursday’s feature, Gravel posted on social media that a top-16 finish would secure the championship. Abreu won Thursday’s feature ahead of Tyler Courtney and Bill Balog, with Kofoid fourth and Garet Williamson fifth. The World Finals continue Friday and conclude Saturday at The Dirt Track at Charlotte, closing the 2026 World of Outlaws season.

body: David Gravel and the Big Game Motorsports No. 2 lead Michael Kofoid by 124 points with only World Finals at Charlotte remaining, according to World of Outlaws. David Gravel and Big Game Motorsports can clinch a third straight championship in the World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series. They hold a 124-point lead over Michael Kofoid with only World Finals left at The Dirt Track at Charlotte Nov. 4-7. Only Steve Kinser, Donny Schatz, and Brad Sweet have gone back-to-back-to-back. Gravel cited consistent qualifying as a key to the team's season. Kofoid and Roth Motorsports are second in the standings.

title: Nov 2: Gravel Eyes Historic Three-Peat at Charlotte World Finals
text: David Gravel and Big Game Motorsports hold a 124-point lead over Michael Kofoid heading into the Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals (Nov. 4-7) at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. David Gravel enters the final week of the 2026 World of Outlaws Sprint Car Series season on…
body: David Gravel and Big Game Motorsports hold a 124-point lead over Michael Kofoid heading into the Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals (Nov. 4-7) at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. David Gravel enters the final week of the 2026 World of Outlaws Sprint Car Series season on the verge of a rare achievement. Through 48 years of Series history, only three drivers have won three consecutive World of Outlaws championships: Steve Kinser, Donny Schatz and Brad Sweet. Gravel and the Big Game Motorsports team, which won its first title together in 2024 and repeated in 2025, can become the fourth at the Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals, Nov. 4-7 at The Dirt Track at Charlotte in Concord, N.C. A third title would also tie Gravel with Sammy Swindell for the fourth-most championships in Series history. The lead has been built on consistency. Gravel and the Tod Quiring-owned No. 2 team have collected 11 wins, 32 podiums and 64 top-10 finishes across 72 starts this season, with an average finish of 5.17. He holds a 124-point advantage over Michael "Buddy" Kofoid of Roth Motorsports, who leads the Series with 17 wins. Sheldon Haudenschild sits third, 222 points back, followed by Carson Macedo at minus-320. Gravel's crew includes crew chief Cody Jacobs, car chief Luke Vaughn and tire specialist Zach Patterson. SPEED SPORT noted that the team's statistics dipped slightly compared with 2025, but the championship remains theirs to lose. The clinch scenario is straightforward. Three Sprint Car Series races remain on the 78-race schedule, all at Charlotte, according to World of Outlaws standings (75 of 78 races complete). Big Game Motorsports stated entering the week, as reported by Speedway Digest, that as long as Gravel finishes 20th or better in each of the three World Finals main events, he will clinch the title. If he falls outside the top 20 in any of the three features, the title would depend on Kofoid's and Haudenschild's results, and the Series has not published scenarios for that case. Charlotte has been one of Gravel's strongest tracks. His eight World of Outlaws wins at The Dirt Track at Charlotte are the second-most by any driver, and half of them have come since he joined Big Game Motorsports. In 14 Charlotte starts in the No. 2, he has finished fourth or better eight times. The four-night World Finals closes the Series' 49th season and also features the World of Outlaws Late Models and the Super DIRTcar Series.

title: Derek Hagar and Howard Moore Win USCS Flip Flop 50 Features as Terry Gray Clinches 17th Title
text: Hagar won the Flip from fifth and Moore won the Flop from 10th at Riverside International Speedway, while Gray clinched his 17th USCS National Championship in the final race of his career. Derek Hagar of Marion, Arkansas, and Howard Moore of Memphis, Tennessee, won the two…
body: Hagar won the Flip from fifth and Moore won the Flop from 10th at Riverside International Speedway, while Gray clinched his 17th USCS National Championship in the final race of his career. Derek Hagar of Marion, Arkansas, and Howard Moore of Memphis, Tennessee, won the two 25-lap features in the 18th annual Ace Doran Bobby Martin Memorial Flip Flop 50 for the United Sprint Car Series at Riverside International Speedway in West Memphis, Arkansas, on Saturday, Nov. 21, according to the official USCS race report and results released by Roby Helm of Helm Communications and posted by Riverside International Speedway. National Sprint Car Hall of Fame inductee Terry Gray of Bartlett, Tennessee, clinched his 17th USCS National Championship in the final race of the 2026 season and retired as an active competitor, according to the report. Gray won the title by 18 points over Jeff Willingham of Ripley, Mississippi, after entering the event with a 22-point lead. Gray was involved in a first-lap multi-car tangle in the Flip and restarted at the tail with a badly bent top wing. He finished 18th in the Flip after starting 10th, and 23rd in the Flop after starting 17th. “It’s been a lot of fun to get here, and I did it the way I wanted to,” Gray said in the report. “I wish my Mom and Dad were here, but I know they’re watching down from above and I have family here tonight.” Hagar started fifth in the Flip, took the lead after contact with leader Gunner Swindell-Herrington on lap 10, and won by 1.537 seconds over Moore, according to the report. Riley Goodno, Brad Bowden and Hayden Martin completed the top five. Polesitter Landon Crawley finished 21st. Morgan Turpen-Havener started 21st and finished ninth to earn the Wilwood Disc Brakes Hard Charger Award. The finish of the Flip set an inverted lineup for the Flop. Conner Wray led from the pole until Moore passed him on lap 21, and Moore won by .787 of a second, according to the report. Wray finished second, Hagar started 23rd and finished third to earn the Hard Charger Award, Bowden was fourth and Keith Ainsworth fifth. The report said Hagar is the only driver to win both races in the event’s 18-year history. In Friday’s preliminary action, Crawley won the 15-lap pole scramble ahead of Swindell-Herrington and Martin, with Gray 10th. Heat races were won by Martin, Hagar, Dusty Young and Moore, and Bowden won Saturday’s 15-lap B-main, according to the official results. The event concluded the 2026 USCS season, the series’ 30th Anniversary Outlaw Thunder Tour. Earlier coverage of Gray’s final start is available on DirtSprintCars.com.

title: Blake Hahn Wins POWRi 410 Season Finale at Texas Motor Speedway
text: Hahn led all 25 laps from the pole on Saturday, Nov. 7, for his first career POWRi Honest Abe Roofing 410 Outlaw Sprint League feature win on Championship Night of Deuces Wild. Blake Hahn closed the 2026 POWRi Honest Abe Roofing 410 Outlaw Sprint League season with a…
body: Hahn led all 25 laps from the pole on Saturday, Nov. 7, for his first career POWRi Honest Abe Roofing 410 Outlaw Sprint League feature win on Championship Night of Deuces Wild. Blake Hahn closed the 2026 POWRi Honest Abe Roofing 410 Outlaw Sprint League season with a wire-to-wire win Saturday, Nov. 7, at Texas Motor Speedway Dirt Track. Starting from the pole as the high-point qualifier, Hahn led every lap of the 25-lap Championship Night feature in Deuces Wild for his first career victory in the series. Austin McCarl, who started fifth, finished second after a late charge. Friday night’s winner Rees Moran was third, with Brenham Crouch fourth and Xavier Doney fifth. SPEED SPORT and STLRacing reported 25 entries. Ryder McCutcheon set quick time in Thursday qualifying at 13.516 seconds and started second; he finished eighth. Heat winners were Moran, Hahn and Justin Henderson. Joe B. Miller was the hard charger, advancing seven positions. Hahn said he tagged the wall early but the car stayed together, then held off McCarl on a late restart by running the high side. “This car was really good tonight. I tagged the wall early and thought I gave it away, but it stayed together,” Hahn said. “I saw Austin coming late, and on that last restart I knew I had to hit my marks on top and just hammer down. A great way to cap off the year and to be able to get a win here at TMS in a 410 is special.”

title: Storms Cancel Hangtown 100 at Placerville; USAC Midgets Resume Nov. 18 at Plaza Park
text: Officials called off both nights, Nov. 13-14, because of a forecast for heavy rain. The decision ends the 2026 season at Placerville Speedway. Hangtown 100 officials canceled both nights of the event, Friday and Saturday, Nov. 13-14, at Placerville Speedway in Placerville,…
body: Officials called off both nights, Nov. 13-14, because of a forecast for heavy rain. The decision ends the 2026 season at Placerville Speedway. Hangtown 100 officials canceled both nights of the event, Friday and Saturday, Nov. 13-14, at Placerville Speedway in Placerville, California, because of the weather forecast, TJ Slideways reported. Tickets will be refunded automatically, less credit card processing fees, and the money is expected in fans’ accounts within 7 to 10 days. No makeup date was announced. “With how the forecast looks for this weekend we wanted to make an early decision since people are traveling from all over,” promoter Scott Russell said. He added that some forecast models showed up to about two inches of rain from Friday into Saturday. The cancellation ends the season at Placerville Speedway. The Hangtown 100 was to open the USAC NOS Energy Drink National Midgets’ seven-race Golden State Invasion and include winged 360 sprint cars. Kyle Larson, a co-promoter of the event with Russell Motorsports, had been announced for both classes. The 2024 Hangtown 100 was also canceled, because of rain and cold, and Daison Pursley won the most recent running, in 2025. USAC’s National Midgets resume Nov. 18 at Plaza Park Raceway in Visalia, according to USAC (that date was later rescheduled for Monday, Nov. 23, according to USAC Media, Nov. 17 ; read the update ). The series then runs two nights at Merced Speedway on Nov. 20-21 and the Jason Leffler Memorial at Bakersfield on Nov. 24.
