title: High Limit Racing Posts Record 69-Night 2027 Schedule
text: The fourth national tour will visit 34 tracks in 19 states, opening March 18–20 at Las Vegas Motor Speedway and closing Oct. 15–16 at Texas Motor Speedway. Interstate Batteries High Limit Racing released a record 69-night schedule for its 2027 national tour on Monday, Nov. 23,…
body: The fourth national tour will visit 34 tracks in 19 states, opening March 18–20 at Las Vegas Motor Speedway and closing Oct. 15–16 at Texas Motor Speedway. Interstate Batteries High Limit Racing released a record 69-night schedule for its 2027 national tour on Monday, Nov. 23, according to a series release. The fourth national season will visit 34 tracks in 19 states, the series said, and all events will be streamed live on FloRacing. The season opens with the Blackjack Bash on Thursday through Saturday, March 18–20, at Las Vegas Motor Speedway and closes with All-In Championship Weekend on Friday and Saturday, Oct. 15–16, at Texas Motor Speedway in Fort Worth. The series said it is committing nearly $10 million to competitors in 2027, including $2,925,000 in High Roller Club payouts to 10 card-holding teams, up to $1,215,000 through the Joker Fund, an additional $132,500 from the Winner Bonus Pool, and more than $5.5 million in nightly purses. The Las Vegas opener is the first of four High Limit races scheduled parallel to a nearby NASCAR event. The others, according to the release, are the Stockyard Stampede on Saturday, May 1, at Texas Motor Speedway, and High Limit shows at Lakeside Speedway in Kansas City, Kansas, on Friday, May 7, and Saturday, Oct. 2, alongside Kansas Speedway events. Port Royal Speedway will host the $100,000-to-win Bob Weikert Memorial on Friday through Sunday, May 28–30, a mid-summer doubleheader on Friday and Saturday, July 23–24, and the $60,000-to-win Tuscarora 50 on Thursday through Saturday, Sept. 9–11, according to the release. During Kings Royal week, High Limit will sanction the Double Down Duels and the $100,000-to-win Joker’s Jackpot on Wednesday and Thursday, July 14–15, at Eldora Speedway in Rossburg, Ohio, and the series returns to Eldora for the 4-Crown Nationals on Sept. 24–25 with USAC Midgets, Sprint Cars and Silver Crown. On the West Coast, the $100,073-to-win Gold Cup Race of Champions is scheduled for Thursday through Saturday, Aug. 26–28, at Silver Dollar Speedway in Chico, California, and the $126,000-to-win Skagit Nationals for Thursday through Saturday, Sept. 2–4, at Skagit Speedway in Alger, Washington. The release said an expanded 12-race West Coast stretch begins Wednesday, Aug. 18, at Santa Maria Speedway and includes the return of national 410 sprint cars to Calistoga Speedway for a doubleheader on Saturday and Sunday, Aug. 21–22. Eight tracks will host their first High Limit events in 2027, the series said: Calistoga; Mansfield Speedway in Mansfield, Ohio, which will run the Freedom 251 on July 2–3, with a High Limit and Lucas Oil Late Model Dirt Series doubleheader on Friday, July 2, and a $51,000-to-win High Limit finale on Saturday, July 3; US-36 Raceway in Osborn, Missouri, on Friday, April 16; I-94 emr Speedway in Fergus Falls, Minnesota, on Thursday, June 10; Granite City Motor Park in Sauk Rapids, Minnesota, on Friday, June 11; Mississippi Thunder Speedway in Fountain City, Wisconsin, on Saturday, June 12; West Virginia Motor Speedway in Mineral Wells, West Virginia, on Saturday, July 10; and Selinsgrove Speedway in Selinsgrove, Pennsylvania, on Thursday, July 22. After a hiatus, 34 Raceway in West Burlington, Iowa, returns on Thursday, April 22, Lake Ozark Speedway in Eldon, Missouri, on Saturday, May 8, and Friday, Oct. 1, and Bridgeport Motorsports Park in Swedesboro, New Jersey, on Tuesday, July 27, according to the release. The release also listed the $55,555-to-win Eagle Nationals on Tuesday, June 8, at Eagle Raceway, the $25,000-to-win Don Martin Memorial Silver Cup on Tuesday, July 20, at Lernerville Speedway in Sarver, Pennsylvania, the $26,000-to-win Rayce Rudeen Foundation Race on Friday and Saturday, May 14–15, at Kokomo Speedway, Lernerville’s Commonwealth Clash on Friday and Saturday, Sept. 17–18, and the 17th annual Jesse Hockett / Daniel McMillin Memorial on Thursday through Saturday, Oct. 7–9, at Lucas Oil Speedway in Wheatland, Missouri, as the penultimate weekend of the season. Vado Speedway Park will expand to a Friday-Saturday doubleheader on April 2–3. Two weekends on the schedule, April 29–30 and May 4–5, are listed as to be determined.

title: High Limit Adopts Controlled Open Tire Rule for 2027
text: Interstate Batteries High Limit Racing will allow teams to choose between designated Hoosier Racing Tire and American Racer compounds at series events next season. Interstate Batteries High Limit Racing will adopt a controlled open tire rule for the 2027 season, allowing teams…
body: Interstate Batteries High Limit Racing will allow teams to choose between designated Hoosier Racing Tire and American Racer compounds at series events next season. Interstate Batteries High Limit Racing will adopt a controlled open tire rule for the 2027 season, allowing teams to choose between and run designated Hoosier Racing Tire and American Racer compounds at series events, the series announced Friday from Mooresville, N.C. The change, published in a High Limit release, will be written into the official 2027 rulebook. “Since the inception of High Limit our first and foremost objective has been the growth and health of Sprint Car Racing as an entirety,” said Brad Sweet, the six-time national champion who founded the series alongside three-time NASCAR Cup Series champion Kyle Larson in 2022. “This was not a decision that we took lightly, but after seeing and feeling the product in action and discussing this with teams, drivers, and vendors, we believe this is the best move for the sport moving forward. The opportunity is now there for both Hoosier Racing Tire and American Racer to create the best product possible and offer competitive prices. Teams are now afforded an extra option, and fans now have another storyline to follow each night and throughout the season.” According to the release, only designated racing tires will be permitted on all four positions at High Limit Sprint Car Series events. Right rear tires must durometer at least 40. Left rear Hoosier tires must durometer at least 35, and left rear American Racers must durometer at least 38. The designated tires listed in the 2027 rulebook language are, for the front, the Hoosier 85/8.0-15 in D12, D15 and D20 and the American Racer 26.0/8.0-15DT in SD-33 and SD-38; for the left rear, the Hoosier 15.0/92-15, 15.0/93-15, 15.0/94-15, 15.0/95-15 and 15.0/96-15 in D12A and the American Racer 28.5/15.0-15BT, 29.0/15.0-15BT, 29.5/15.0-15BT, 30.0/15.0-15BT and 30.5/15.0-15BT in SD38; and for the right rear, the Hoosier 105/16.0-15 in D15A and Medium, the Hoosier 105/18.0-15 in D15A and RD20A, and the American Racer 34.0/17.0-15GT in SD40/MC2. High Limit said Hoosier, owned by Continental, has been the predominant tire manufacturer in sprint car racing for the past 14 years and will remain an option. With American Racer also permitted, the series said 2027 will mark the first time since 2010-12, when Goodyear was used with the World of Outlaws, that a tire company other than Hoosier is allowed at the top level of the sport. Officials plan to work directly with national and local vendors for both brands to supply as much product as possible at sanctioned events, the release said.

title: Scelzi wins Texas finale, Abreu clinches High Limit title
text: Giovanni Scelzi swept the High Limit finale weekend, but Rico Abreu held off his late charge to win a second straight series championship. Giovanni Scelzi won both nights at Texas Motor Speedway to close the 2026 Interstate Batteries High Limit Racing season. Rico Abreu won the…
body: Giovanni Scelzi swept the High Limit finale weekend, but Rico Abreu held off his late charge to win a second straight series championship. Giovanni Scelzi won both nights at Texas Motor Speedway to close the 2026 Interstate Batteries High Limit Racing season. Rico Abreu won the championship. Friday, October 16. Scelzi started seventh in the 25-lap feature and worked his way forward. Tanner Holmes led the first 12 laps, then Abreu, who started third, took over and led laps 13 through 17. Scelzi moved into second on lap 16 and passed Abreu for the lead on lap 18, then led the final eight laps. Tyler Courtney, who rose from 11th after an engine change, finished second and took the hard charger award. Abreu was third, followed by Tanner Thorson and Daison Pursley. The win cut Scelzi's deficit in the standings from 45 points to 36 going into Saturday. Saturday, October 17. Scelzi started on the pole and led all 30 laps of the finale, worth $25,000. Abreu stayed on his tail the whole way, trailing by 0.016 seconds with two laps to go, and finished second, 0.202 seconds behind. Brent Marks, Thorson and Courtney completed the top five. Second place was enough. Abreu won the championship by 31 points over Scelzi, his second straight title and his first driving the Carquest Auto Parts No. 24 for Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing. Scelzi, driving for Spire Motorsports in his first full-time High Limit season, won his third straight race, counting his earlier win at Lakeside, and took home $50,000 for the Texas weekend. He finished with a series-best 43 top-10s.

body: The third annual event at Kwinana Beach, Western Australia, pays $20,000 to win each preliminary night and $120,000 to win the finale, a new Australian record, according to High Limit Racing. Buddy Kofoid finished third, with Cole Macedo and Luke Oldfield completing the top five. High Limit announced the 2026 dates and purse that night. Perth Motorplex said the first two editions drew sellout crowds. Three-day tickets are on sale through the track. title: Jack McCarthy Wins Murray Bridge 360/LS Track Championship Round 2
text: McCarthy started from the pole and led throughout Saturday at Murray Bridge Speedway in Murray Bridge, South Australia. The 360/LS feature was declared on lap 22 because of a curfew after Friday rain left the track greasy. Tate Cowie finished second and Hayden Vickers third.…
body: McCarthy started from the pole and led throughout Saturday at Murray Bridge Speedway in Murray Bridge, South Australia. The 360/LS feature was declared on lap 22 because of a curfew after Friday rain left the track greasy. Tate Cowie finished second and Hayden Vickers third. Jack McCarthy won Round 2 of the Lewiston Haulage Murray Bridge Speedway 360/LS Track Championship on Saturday, Nov. 14, at Murray Bridge Speedway in Murray Bridge, South Australia, according to a report posted on the track website. McCarthy, who had won the South Australian Speedcar Championship two weeks earlier, started the feature from the pole after a heat win and a runner-up finish and was not headed. Tate Cowie of Kadina finished second, and Hayden Vickers was third. The track received a substantial amount of rain Friday, and the report said the surface was extremely greasy all evening, with turn two the most troublesome. The round drew 14 entries for three heats and the feature. McCarthy won heat 1 ahead of Hilton Rowett and Corey Sandow. Sandow, driving one of only two 360-cubic-inch powered cars in the field, then beat McCarthy and Brodie Somerfield in heat 2. Cowie won heat 3 over Vickers and Sam Martin. That put McCarthy and Sandow on the front row, followed by Cowie, Vickers, Somerfield, Rowett, Keke Falland, Martin, Round 1 winner Luke Squiers, Erin Virgin, Isla Rowett, Jack Will and Zack Sloan. McCarthy led Sandow and Cowie early until a red flag on lap 4, when Sandow clashed with Will’s slower car. Sandow restarted at the rear and later retired. McCarthy then led Cowie and Vickers, with the three remaining close in lapped traffic, the report said. The race ended on lap 22 when Martin spun in turn two and brought out a caution. With a curfew approaching, officials declared the finish. The track report said it was the second straight 360/LS sprint car feature at Murray Bridge that did not go the scheduled distance. Hilton Rowett finished fourth, followed by Somerfield, Squiers, Virgin, Sloan, Martin and Isla Rowett.

body: The 2027 schedule includes five 410 sprint car shows and closes with the World of Outlaws at the 49th annual Jackson Nationals on Aug. 20–21. title: James McFadden Wins Australian Sprintcar Championship Night 1 at Toowoomba
text: McFadden beat Ryan Newton by 1.03 seconds in Friday’s Preliminary A Main at Hi-Tec Oils Toowoomba Speedway. Brock Hallett finished third. Lachlan McHugh leads the points into Saturday’s finale. James McFadden won the Preliminary A Main on Night 1 of the 64th Nutrend Homes…
body: McFadden beat Ryan Newton by 1.03 seconds in Friday’s Preliminary A Main at Hi-Tec Oils Toowoomba Speedway. Brock Hallett finished third. Lachlan McHugh leads the points into Saturday’s finale. James McFadden won the Preliminary A Main on Night 1 of the 64th Nutrend Homes Australian Sprintcar Championship on Friday, Nov. 20, at Hi-Tec Oils Toowoomba Speedway in Toowoomba, Queensland, according to Speedcafe. McFadden, driving the WX23, beat Ryan Newton (Q66) by 1.03 seconds. Brock Hallett (Q5) finished third, Lachlan McHugh (NQ7) fourth and Liam Williams (NQ26) fifth. Speedcafe reported McFadden is chasing a fourth Australian title, and that this is the first time Toowoomba has hosted the championship. McHugh started from the pole and led most of the race, Speedcafe said. He had posted quick time in qualifying at 11.135 seconds and won his first heat. The yellow came out after one lap when Preliminary B Main winner Marcus Dumesny made contact with Henry Titman in turn 1, slowing up and catching Kaiden Manders. After a restart, the race was stopped when Randy Morgan spun in turn 4 and Brendan Quinn’s car caught fire in the paddock. McHugh led again with 12 laps to go before Jy Corbet found the wall in turn 4, climbed the concrete and flipped, collecting Matthew Dumesny, according to the report. With six laps remaining, McFadden passed McHugh on the inside into turn 4. Speedcafe said McHugh’s car then tightened on corner exit and moved toward the inside wall, and that Hallett and Newton joined the fight as McHugh dropped from the lead to fourth in the space of a lap. Newton had charged from outside the top 10. The race ran green for the final 11 laps. Luke Oldfield (Q17) finished sixth, Aaron Kelly (Q7) seventh and Dumesny (N47) eighth. Reigning champion Jock Goodyer (A1), who transferred from the B Main and raced forward from the rear of the A Main, finished ninth after circulating with a flattening left rear tire under the last caution. Harry Stewart (Q96) was 10th. McHugh leads the Night 1 points with 809, five ahead of Hallett (804), Speedcafe reported. McFadden and Williams are tied for third with 796, followed by Oldfield (783) and Kelly (772). The top six in points after Night 1 advance directly to the qualifying dash for the A Main and do not have to run further heat races. The championship finale is scheduled for Saturday, Nov. 21, at Toowoomba.

title: Jason Martin Healthy and Open to Driving or Crew Roles After DJ Bybee Steps Back
text: Martin says he is fully recovered after sitting out 2026 and open to driving, crew, or team opportunities. BM Motorsports is not closing. Jason Martin says he is fully recovered and open to driving, crew, or team opportunities after DJ Bybee stepped back from BM Motorsports.…
body: Martin says he is fully recovered after sitting out 2026 and open to driving, crew, or team opportunities. BM Motorsports is not closing. Jason Martin says he is fully recovered and open to driving, crew, or team opportunities after DJ Bybee stepped back from BM Motorsports. Martin announced the change Monday. Bybee, a longtime partner and primary sponsor, is shifting his focus to growing Bybee Electric. Martin thanked Bybee and said the partnership was built on friendship as well as racing. Martin, a longtime 360 sprint car driver based in the Lincoln, Nebraska area, is the 2023 American Sprint Car Series National Tour champion. He has more than 100 career feature wins and has raced in 34 states and Canada. He and Bybee formed BM Motorsports in 2017. Martin sat out the 2026 season after injuries sustained in April. He wrote that he is “100% healed” and “ready to get back behind the wheel.” During the year off he worked as crew chief while Jake Bubak drove the car. He is open to: Driving for an established team A hired mechanic, crew chief, or team management role A funded driver joining the existing BM Motorsports program Martin said the team is not closing. “This isn’t about closing a chapter on racing. It’s about being open-minded, finding the right opportunities, and figuring out the best way to keep doing what I love.”

body: Petty Performance Racing’s national sprint car team will not continue into 2027. After Kyle Cummins clinched his second straight USAC AMSOIL National Sprint Car Championship in 2026, team owner Jerry Petty announced that Petty Performance Racing’s national sprint car team will not continue into 2027. Petty described it as “going out on top.” Cummins and Petty Performance Racing won the 2025 and 2026 USAC National Sprint Car titles together, including 11 wins in 2026 alone in the No. 3p. Petty isn’t leaving the sport. He continues to sponsor USAC CRA Sprint Cars and Western States Midgets, supports major events including the BC39 and the Corn Belt Clash, stays involved with Central Arizona Raceway, and backs youth development programs.

Jett Yantis of Bakersfield, California, won the 40-lap Good Earth Farms Special Presented by Peelz, the first USAC NOS Energy Drink Midget National Championship feature at Plaza Park Raceway in Visalia, California, on Monday, Nov. 23, according to official USAC results. body: Drake clinched his first national midget title for RMS Racing on the final weekend at I-44 Speedway and finished 310 points ahead of Karter Sarff. Kale Drake of Collinsville, Oklahoma, won the 2026 POWRi National Midget League championship driving for RMS Racing, POWRi announced Oct. 26. It is the first national midget title for both Drake and RMS Racing, according to Toyota. Drake, who won the POWRi Micro League title in 2023, is the first driver to win both the POWRi National Midget and Micro League championships, according to the league. Drake clinched the title with a fourth-place finish in the Oct. 23 feature at I-44 Speedway in Oklahoma City, the first night of the season-ending weekend, Toyota Racing reported. Brecken Reese led all 30 laps to win that race. The championship became official after the Oct. 24 finale, in which Drake set quick time and started on the front row but was involved in a rollover on the opening lap and finished 22nd. Gaige Weldon won the finale. In 21 starts, Drake had his first four POWRi National Midget feature wins, 16 top-five finishes, 18 top-10 finishes and five runner-up finishes, according to POWRi. He also led the league with eight heat race wins and added a stand-alone POWRi West Midget win. Drake finished 310 points ahead of Karter Sarff of Mason City, Illinois. Kyle Jones of Kennedale, Texas, was third, 600 points back, followed by Reese, 820 back, and Drake Edwards, 1,310 back. The title qualifies Drake for the Race of Champions at the Chili Bowl Nationals. It is the third straight POWRi national midget title for a Toyota-powered driver, after Cannon McIntosh in 2024 and Jacob Denney in 2025, Toyota said. Drake is also sixth in the USAC National Midget standings with 941 points heading into the series’ five-race California finish, which starts Nov. 18 at Plaza Park Raceway (that date was rescheduled for Monday, Nov. 23, according to USAC Media, Nov. 17 ; read the update ). title: Kalib Henry Joins Beaver Racing for 2027 POWRi 410 Season
text: The 27-year-old from Sacramento, California, will drive the No. 12X Maxim powered by Don Ott Racing Engines. Henry is leaving Jim Muth’s Racers for Life No. 101 after back-to-back All Star Circuit of Champions titles. Kalib Henry will join Beaver Racing beginning in 2027,…
body: The 27-year-old from Sacramento, California, will drive the No. 12X Maxim powered by Don Ott Racing Engines. Henry is leaving Jim Muth’s Racers for Life No. 101 after back-to-back All Star Circuit of Champions titles. Kalib Henry will join Beaver Racing beginning in 2027, according to a release posted Nov. 18 on Kalib Henry Racing’s website. The 27-year-old from Sacramento, California, will drive the No. 12X Maxim powered by Don Ott Racing Engines. Henry and Beaver Racing will race for a POWRi 410 Outlaw Sprint League championship and in select World of Outlaws and High Limit Racing events, the release said. Henry is coming off his second consecutive All Star Circuit of Champions driver’s championship, which he clinched with a second-place finish in the season finale Oct. 3 at Michaels Mercer Raceway Park, according to SPEED SPORT. Henry is leaving Jim Muth’s Racers for Life No. 101, which he first drove at the 2023 Knoxville Nationals and then full-time for the past three seasons, the release said. “I’m excited to join Beaver Racing for 2027,” Henry said. “Billy and Cheryl Vielhauer have been amazing to work with as everything began to fall into place. They have worked relentlessly to not only ensure Bob’s [Vielhauer] legacy lives on but to field a competitive team that can compete for wins at any level. I am honored they believe in me to drive their race car and excited to get to work and grow with them next year and beyond.” In that span, Henry recorded 16 wins, 50 top-fives and 72 top-10s, according to the release. He won six features and the Fremont Speedway 410 track championship in 2024, then followed in 2025 with five wins and his first All Star driver’s championship. In 2026 he defended the All Star title with four wins and claimed the team’s first All Star owner’s championship, the release said. He also started the Kings Royal main event in 2026. His 2026 U.S. record was 37 races, four wins, 14 top-fives and 20 top-10s. Henry thanked Muth and crew chief Andy Potter in the announcement. “I want to personally thank Jim ‘Doc’ Muth for the opportunity to pilot the Racers for Life No. 101 starting at the 2023 Knoxville Nationals and then full-time for the last three years,” Henry said. “His commitment to the team’s success was pivotal, and I will forever be grateful for what we built together.” Beaver Racing is a family-owned team based in Shawnee, Kansas, started in 1980 by Bob “Beaver” Vielhauer, a 2022 Knoxville Raceway Hall of Fame inductee. The operation is now led by Billy and Cheryl Vielhauer and their daughter Samantha, the release said. In 2026 the team recorded a victory, six top-fives and 11 top-10s competing with the POWRi 410 Outlaw Sprint League. “We’re excited to welcome Kalib to the team!” Beaver Racing said. “He has really proven himself through his success racing with the All Stars and has consistently shown the hard work and dedication it takes to compete. We can’t wait to see him bring that same work ethic, drive, and determination to the 12X. We’re looking forward to what the future holds and are excited to have him as part of the team!” The release said full details of team partners and the 2027 schedule will be announced later.

title: Nov. 4, 1945: Kenny Weld Is Born in Kansas City
text: Kenny Weld won the Knoxville Nationals at 18, went on to win it four times, captured three Williams Grove National Opens and later built the “Batmobile” modified and the Weld Tech business. Kenneth Eugene Weld was born Nov. 4, 1945, in Kansas City, Missouri, into a racing…
body: Kenny Weld won the Knoxville Nationals at 18, went on to win it four times, captured three Williams Grove National Opens and later built the “Batmobile” modified and the Weld Tech business. Kenneth Eugene Weld was born Nov. 4, 1945, in Kansas City, Missouri, into a racing family. He started racing in 1961 at Riverside and Lakeside Speedways, moving from jalopies to sportsman cars and then to super modifieds in 1962, according to the Eastern Motorsport Press Association. In 1964, at 18, he won the Knoxville Nationals. Teamed with his father, Taylor “Pappy” Weld, in a car known as the “Tank,” he won the event again in 1965. He returned from Pennsylvania to win two more Nationals in 1972 and 1973 for car owner Bob Weikert, giving him four Knoxville Nationals titles in nine starts, according to The Third Turn. By the late 1960s Weld had moved east and became one of the leading outlaw sprint car drivers before the World of Outlaws formed in 1978. In 1970 he won 27 features and the Williams Grove championship in Bud Grimm’s car, and in 1974 he won 39 features and a record fifth Williams Grove championship, according to EMPA. The Third Turn credits him with three wins in seven starts in the Williams Grove National Open, along with a win in the Tuscarora 50. In 1975 he moved to big-block modifieds and won 16 races driving for Weikert at Reading. Weld’s influence extended to car building. In 1980 he built, with Don Brown, the modified known as the “Batmobile” for Gary Balough. Balough won at Syracuse with it, and the rules were changed to keep cars like it from racing again. Weld retired from driving after a crash at Buckeye Speedway in Ohio in 1988 and founded Weld Tech with his brother Greg and his daughter Debra; the business became known for cylinder-head porting. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 1997 and died March 20, 1997, after a two-year battle with cancer. The Weld family is well represented in the Hall. Greg Weld, the 1963 Knoxville Nationals winner and 1967 USAC sprint car champion, was inducted in 1998, and Pappy Weld, who started the family’s open-wheel tradition by building and owning a midget in the 1930s, was inducted in 2006.

title: Dayne Kingshott Wins WA Sprintcar Title at Bunbury
text: Kingshott led all 35 laps from second at Bunbury Speedway on Nov. 7, delivering Krikke Motorsport its ninth Western Australian Sprintcar Championship and his second title. Dayne Kingshott won the Western Australian Sprintcar Championship on Saturday, Nov. 7, at Bunbury Speedway,…
body: Kingshott led all 35 laps from second at Bunbury Speedway on Nov. 7, delivering Krikke Motorsport its ninth Western Australian Sprintcar Championship and his second title. Dayne Kingshott won the Western Australian Sprintcar Championship on Saturday, Nov. 7, at Bunbury Speedway, leading every lap of the 35-lap feature after starting second. The result was Krikke Motorsport’s ninth WA title and the team’s first win of the 2026-27 season. It was Kingshott’s second WA title. He previously won the championship at Perth Motorplex in the 2022-23 season. Auto Action and the team said it was also his first victory with Krikke Motorsport at the team’s home track. He drove the Mobil 1 and Bunbury Toyota-backed Maxim, the WA No. 2. Callum Williamson finished second, followed by Kaiden Manders, Kris Coyle and Daniel Harding. Kingshott said, “It was awesome to win another Western Australian Title for the Krikke Motorsport team and what made it even more special for all of us was that it was our first win together at Bunbury.” He added that winning at the home track “hits differently” because of family, friends and local sponsors. Team manager Ryan Krikke said he was pleased to get the team’s first win together at Bunbury and another Western Australian title. He said the team has had a good start to the season “but just haven’t got a lot to show for it so far,” and hoped the title win would build momentum toward a fourth Maddington Toyota Sprintcar Series championship. Kingshott sits seventh in the MTSS standings heading into Saturday’s King of Wings at Perth Motorplex, an event he has won the past three years.

We continue to focus on filling the grandstands each year and allow those who can’t be at the track to have the best viewing experience no matter where they are through DIRTVision’s growing platform,” said Brian Carter, World Racing Group CEO. “We look forward to further enhancing the at-track and at-home viewing experience every year.” “We are extremely pleased to extend our partnership with the World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series and DIRTVision,” said Knoxville Raceway General Manager Jason Reed. “DIRTVision has played an important role in connecting our fans, race teams, and marketing partners. title: Kyle Cummins Wins Second Straight USAC National Sprint Car Title
text: Cummins clinched the 2026 title Oct. 22 at Central Arizona Raceway with two races left. He won a career-high 11 features and finished 183 points ahead of Justin Grant. Kyle Cummins of Princeton, Indiana, won the 2026 USAC AMSOIL National Sprint Car championship, his second…
body: Cummins clinched the 2026 title Oct. 22 at Central Arizona Raceway with two races left. He won a career-high 11 features and finished 183 points ahead of Justin Grant. Kyle Cummins of Princeton, Indiana, won the 2026 USAC AMSOIL National Sprint Car championship, his second straight series title. He clinched it Oct. 22 with a third-place finish in the Western World Championships opener at Central Arizona Raceway in Casa Grande, Arizona, with two races left, USAC reported. The result also gave Petty Performance Racing its second straight entrant title with the No. 3p. Cummins finished with 3,333 points, 183 ahead of Justin Grant (3,150), according to USAC’s final standings. Mitchel Moles was third with 3,075, Jake Swanson fourth with 2,873 and Kevin Thomas Jr. fifth with 2,657. Cummins led the series with a career-high 11 wins and 351 laps led in 48 starts, and he tied Grant for the most top-10 finishes with 45. Cummins took the points lead in the eighth race of the season, in early April, and kept it the rest of the year. He set a USAC National Sprint Car record with 45 consecutive top-10 finishes, breaking the mark of 29 set by Thomas in 2025. His wins included his first USAC victories at the Terre Haute Action Track half-mile, in April’s Jim Hurtubise Classic; at Eldora Speedway, in May; and at Knoxville Raceway, in May’s Corn Belt Clash. He returned to Eldora in September to win the 4-Crown Nationals, and he also won the Indiana Sprint Week and Eastern Storm titles. “I think I’m more excited about this one than I was the first one,” Cummins told USAC. “I was always saying that just one would be cool. You can have a lucky year and it felt like everything went our way last year. To come out this year and back it up, I don’t know if everything went our way, but we definitely had a really good season.” Shortly after the final race, Petty Performance Racing announced its national team would shut down and not continue into 2027, USAC reported. Cummins is pursuing ownership and partnership options to keep the team together for 2027, DirtSprintCars.com reported Nov. 6 .

title: Lachlan McHugh Wins Australian Sprintcar Title Prelude at Toowoomba
text: McHugh won the 35-lap Prelude to the Title at Hi-Tec Oils Toowoomba Speedway by 1.12 seconds over Ryan Newton, who started 11th. Brock Hallett finished third. The 64th Australian Sprintcar Championship follows Friday and Saturday at Toowoomba. Lachlan McHugh won the Prelude to…
body: McHugh won the 35-lap Prelude to the Title at Hi-Tec Oils Toowoomba Speedway by 1.12 seconds over Ryan Newton, who started 11th. Brock Hallett finished third. The 64th Australian Sprintcar Championship follows Friday and Saturday at Toowoomba. Lachlan McHugh won the Prelude to the Title on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at Hi-Tec Oils Toowoomba Speedway in Toowoomba, Queensland, according to Speedcafe. The 2024 Australian champion, driving the NQ7, beat Ryan Newton (Q66) by 1.12 seconds after Newton charged from 11th on the grid. Brock Hallett (Q5) finished third, James McFadden (WX23) recovered from a lap 1 incident to finish fourth, and Brendan Quinn (S37) was fifth. Speedcafe reported it was McHugh’s 40th feature win at Toowoomba. Marcus Dumesny led early in the 35-lap feature, with McHugh running second. A yellow came out after one lap when Dylan Menz slid down from the top in turn 4 and made contact with Alex Attard, collecting McFadden, Mick Saller and Nic Whell. McFadden was push-started and continued, while Saller and Whell were out. McHugh caught Dumesny with eight laps to go, and with three laps remaining Dumesny tagged the outside wall exiting turn 2, then hit the wall heavily at turn 3 and was out of the race, according to the report. McHugh led the restart, and a third stoppage came on the final lap when Menz hit the wall in turn 1. McHugh pulled away from Newton on the final restart. As the checkered flag fell, B Main winner Randy Morgan slid into the turn 4 wall and rolled against the catch fence; he was classified 10th. Max Guilford finished sixth from the front row, followed by Jy Corbet, Luke Oldfield and Aaron Kelly. The Prelude was a standalone race meeting held in place of an official practice night. The 64th Nutrend Homes Australian Sprintcar Championship runs Friday and Saturday, Nov. 20–21, at Toowoomba, the first time the venue has hosted the title.

body: NASCAR Cup Series driver Kyle Larson will pull double duty in the USAC NOS Energy Drink National Midgets and winged 360 Sprint Cars at the Hangtown 100, Nov. 13-14 at Placerville Speedway. Larson, an Elk Grove, California, native and co-promoter of the Hangtown 100 with Russell Motorsports since 2025, will race both divisions each day at the quarter-mile dirt oval. He has four Hangtown 100 USAC National Midget feature wins at Placerville, in 2019, 2021 and both nights in 2023, according to USAC. FloRacing reported the commitment on Nov. 3. Placerville holds early landmarks in Larson’s dirt career. He made his first Sprint Car start there in 2007 and scored his first Sprint Car win at the track later that season. He also clinched the 2010 Golden State KWS-NARC Series championship at Placerville. The Hangtown 100 schedule features two days of USAC National Midget competition, capped by Saturday’s 100-lap, $10,000-to-win finale. Winged 360 Sprint Cars race both days, with $2,000 to each feature winner. Grandstand gates open at 1 p.m. PT and racing is scheduled for 2 p.m. PT Friday and Saturday. text: Francis, half of the father-son team behind Francis Recovery Buggies, had been part of POWRi race-day operations since the series began, POWRi said. Leo Francis has retired after 21 years with POWRi Racing, the series announced Saturday, Nov. 14. POWRi said Francis had been a…
body: Francis, half of the father-son team behind Francis Recovery Buggies, had been part of POWRi race-day operations since the series began, POWRi said. Leo Francis has retired after 21 years with POWRi Racing, the series announced Saturday, Nov. 14. POWRi said Francis had been a familiar face and an integral part of its race-day operations from the series’ first day. Francis and his son are the father-son team behind Francis Recovery Buggies, which POWRi called a staple in its history. According to the series, Leo played a key role in building the machines that have served the sport for decades. In that role, Francis pushed off and towed drivers ranging from future stars getting their start to established names in the sport, POWRi said. The series credited him with treating every driver, team and piece of equipment with care and with doing whatever it took to keep a race night moving. “People like Leo are the backbone of grassroots racing,” the announcement said. POWRi tagged the announcement to its National Midget, West Midget, WAR Sprint and 410 Outlaw Sprint series. It did not say who will take over his duties.

title: Carson Macedo Wheels from Row Four to World Finals Finale Victory
text: Carson Macedo charged from eighth to win Saturday's $25,000 World of Outlaws season finale at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. Michael Kofoid finished second; Giovanni Scelzi was third. David Gravel is the 2026 champion. Carson Macedo and Jason Johnson Racing closed the 2026 World…
body: Carson Macedo charged from eighth to win Saturday's $25,000 World of Outlaws season finale at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. Michael Kofoid finished second; Giovanni Scelzi was third. David Gravel is the 2026 champion. Carson Macedo and Jason Johnson Racing closed the 2026 World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series season in style. Starting eighth in the 25-lap, $25,000-to-win Dave Smith Motors World Finals feature at The Dirt Track at Charlotte, Macedo worked his way forward, took the lead with a slide job on Giovanni Scelzi on Lap 17, then held off a late challenge from Michael Kofoid to take the checkered flag by 0.324 seconds. Scelzi, who had led the first 16 laps from the pole, finished third. Buddy Schweibinz and Steven Snyder Jr. completed the top five. David Gravel, who clinched his third consecutive championship earlier in the weekend, finished 17th. It was Macedo's eighth World of Outlaws win of the season and the 66th of his career, tying him with Bobby Davis Jr. and Craig Dollansky for 14th all-time. It was also the 90th World of Outlaws victory for Jason Johnson Racing. Macedo called it a great way to end a season that didn't go exactly as planned for the team. The World Finals wrapped a season that saw David Gravel become just the fourth driver to win three straight World of Outlaws Sprint Car titles.

title: Nov. 4, 1998: Mark Kinser Wins Channellock Fall Classic at Las Vegas
text: Mark Kinser held off Australian Peter Murphy to win the inaugural Channellock Fall Classic, the season finale of the 1998 Pennzoil World of Outlaws Series, as cousin Steve Kinser celebrated his 15th series championship. Mark Kinser won the 30-lap A-Feature of the inaugural…
body: Mark Kinser held off Australian Peter Murphy to win the inaugural Channellock Fall Classic, the season finale of the 1998 Pennzoil World of Outlaws Series, as cousin Steve Kinser celebrated his 15th series championship. Mark Kinser won the 30-lap A-Feature of the inaugural Channellock Fall Classic on Wednesday, Nov. 4, 1998, at Las Vegas Motor Speedway, the finale of the Pennzoil World of Outlaws Series’ 20th anniversary season, according to a series race report by Richard Day published by The Auto Channel. The victory, in the #5M Wirtgen Maxim, was Kinser’s 12th A-Feature win of the season, ran his winning streak to three and was his fourth straight victory at Las Vegas Motor Speedway, the report said. Peter Murphy finished second, followed by Sammy Swindell, Danny Lasoski and Steve Kinser, according to the report and The Third Turn’s event results. Kinser started on the pole after winning the Channellock Dash, his 14th dash win of the year, and led the first 17 laps, according to the report. Murphy, the Vivarin Fast-Time Award winner, started inside the fifth row, worked forward and passed Kinser for the lead late in lap 18. Murphy led through lap 25 before Kinser regained the lead and led the final five laps, finishing 3.608 seconds ahead. The report described Murphy’s runner-up finish as the best by an Australian driver in series history. “I wasn’t saving anything,” Kinser said, according to the report. “I changed my line on the last restart and I feel fortunate to be here.” The finale also marked the end of the championship chase. Steve Kinser’s Quaker State team celebrated his 15th Pennzoil World of Outlaws Series drivers’ championship at the track, and the report said he was the first driver/owner to win both titles in the same year. Earlier in the week, the Las Vegas Sun reported that Mark Kinser had won a Channellock Fall Classic A-Feature at the LVMS half-mile on Tuesday night, and that his 12th feature win of the season was not enough to overtake his cousin in the points standings. “Vegas has been really good to us,” Mark Kinser told the Sun. Rounding out the top 10 on Nov. 4 were Terry McCarl, Gary Wright, Stevie Smith, Dale Blaney and Donny Schatz, according to the race report. The race was taped for broadcast on TNN’s Motor Madness program.

title: Tyler Nelson Repeats as USAC Midwest Thunder SpeeD2 Midget Champion
text: The Olathe, Kansas driver won three features and finished 40 points ahead of Bryce Massingill in the 13-race series, becoming the third driver to win consecutive Midwest Thunder titles. Tyler Nelson of Olathe, Kansas successfully defended his USAC Midwest Thunder SpeeD2 Midget…
body: The Olathe, Kansas driver won three features and finished 40 points ahead of Bryce Massingill in the 13-race series, becoming the third driver to win consecutive Midwest Thunder titles. Tyler Nelson of Olathe, Kansas successfully defended his USAC Midwest Thunder SpeeD2 Midget championship in 2026. The 29-year-old won three features in the 13-race series, added a series-leading 10 top-five finishes, 13 top-10s, three fast qualifying times and seven heat-race wins, and beat Bryce Massingill of Troy, Ohio by 40 points in the final standings, 941-901. Nelson had finished fourth at Moler Raceway Park, third at Lawrenceburg Speedway and second at Lincoln Park Speedway in 2025. This year he won at all three tracks and quadrupled his career win total from one to four. In May at Williamsburg, Ohio’s Moler Raceway Park, he led all 25 laps in wire-to-wire fashion and won by 6.054 seconds. In August at Lawrenceburg, in a result he called “the biggest win of my career,” he charged from seventh to first in the first two laps. In September at Putnamville, Indiana’s Lincoln Park Speedway, he went from fifth to first in the next-to-last race and took the point lead for good. Nelson locked up the title with a fifth-place finish in the October finale at Montpelier Speedway. He became the third driver in the 11-year history of the series to win consecutive championships, following Aaron Leffel (2017, 2018 and 2019) and Jacob Denney (2020 and 2021). The point lead had changed hands among Nelson, Matt Lux and Massingill for much of the season. Massingill finished in the top three of the standings for the sixth year in a row and was the runner-up in 2026. The series’ all-time winningest driver, with 23 victories, added five more wins in the latter half of the year — two at Moler, plus Millstream, Circle City and Montpelier — after a 364-night winless stretch, and led a series-high 96 laps. Lux finished third. Kole Kirkman was named Rookie of the Year after finishing sixth. Six drivers started all 13 points-paying features: Stratton Briggs, Buddy Hollmeyer, Massingill, Nelson, Parker Perry and Brayden Schwartz.

title: D.J. Netto Wins Tribute to Gary Patterson; Justyn Cox Claims Second SCCT Title
text: Netto started second and won the Nov. 7 finale at the Stockton Dirt Track. Cox finished third to wrap up his second tour championship. D.J. Netto of Hanford, California, won the Elk Grove Ford Sprint Car Challenge Tour season finale, the Tribute to Gary Patterson, on Saturday,…
body: Netto started second and won the Nov. 7 finale at the Stockton Dirt Track. Cox finished third to wrap up his second tour championship. D.J. Netto of Hanford, California, won the Elk Grove Ford Sprint Car Challenge Tour season finale, the Tribute to Gary Patterson, on Saturday, Nov. 7, at the Stockton Dirt Track. The series said Netto started second in the Netto AG No. 88n and scored his second career Tribute to Gary Patterson victory, worth $5,000 with additional money from Noceti Group Inc. It was the fifth SCCT win of his career, tying him with Colby Copeland for fifth on the tour’s all-time list. Officials shortened the main event to 25 laps after multiple red flags and cautions, according to the series recap. Pole sitter Carson Hammes, who had won the High Sierra Industries Dash, flipped at the start of the feature and brought out a red flag. The series said Hammes was uninjured but finished for the night. After the race was shortened, Netto led the rest of the way and lapped up to sixth place. Shane Golobic of Fremont, California, finished second. Justyn Cox finished third and clinched his second Elk Grove Ford Sprint Car Challenge Tour championship. The series said Cox had two wins, eight top-five finishes and 12 top-10s on the way to the title. Jake Morgan finished fourth and Dylan Bloomfield fifth. Completing the top 10 were Andy Forsberg, Cole Croft, Jake Haulot, Dawson Hammes and hard charger Kenny Wanderstadt, who started 24th. Jett Barnes of Visalia set a new 360 track record at Stockton with a lap of 11.230, the series said.

body: Saturated grounds and a forecast for more rain called off the Wednesday, Nov. 18, Good Earth Farms Special at Visalia, Calif. The Golden State Invasion resumes Nov. 20-21 at Merced Speedway. The Wednesday, Nov. 18, debut of USAC NOS Energy Drink Midget National Championship racing at Plaza Park Raceway in Visalia, California, has been postponed because of saturated grounds and a forecast calling for more rain leading into race day, USAC announced on Nov. 16. Plaza Park Raceway and USAC officials are working on details to potentially reschedule the Good Earth Farms Special Presented by Peelz at the 1/5-mile dirt oval during this month’s Golden State Invasion, according to USAC. No new date had been announced. USAC said updates will be posted on its website and social media pages and on Plaza Park Raceway’s. The Golden State Invasion continues Friday and Saturday, Nov. 20-21, at Merced Speedway, followed by Tuesday, Nov. 24, at Bakersfield Speedway at Kevin Harvick’s Kern Raceway and Saturday, Nov. 28, at Ventura Raceway, USAC said.

body: The Good Earth Farms Special, postponed from Wednesday, Nov. 18, because of rain, will be run Monday night at Visalia, Calif. It is round three of the Golden State Invasion and USAC’s national debut at the 1/5-mile oval. USAC has rescheduled the first USAC NOS Energy Drink Midget National Championship event at Plaza Park Raceway in Visalia, California, for Monday night, Nov. 23, the series announced Nov. 17. The original Wednesday, Nov. 18, date for the Good Earth Farms Special Presented by Peelz was postponed because of rain, according to USAC. The Plaza Park event will be round three of USAC’s Golden State Invasion and marks the series’ national debut at the 1/5-mile dirt oval, USAC said. A-Class Micros are also on the card. On race day, the pits open at 3:30 p.m. Pacific, the front gate opens at 5 p.m., the drivers meeting is at 5:15 p.m. and hot laps begin at 6 p.m., followed by qualifying and racing, according to USAC. Advance tickets are on sale at plazaparkraceway.com or on the Ticket Hoss app, and tickets will also be sold at the gate. Adult general admission (ages 13 and up) is $30, senior and military general admission are $20, children ages 4 and under are free, and pit passes are $45, USAC said. The Golden State Invasion consists of five USAC NOS Energy Drink Midget National Championship events in California, starting Friday and Saturday, Nov. 20-21, with the Chase Johnson Classic at Merced Speedway, then continuing at Plaza Park on Monday, Nov. 23, according to USAC. The series then goes to Bakersfield Speedway at Kevin Harvick’s Kern Raceway on Tuesday, Nov. 24, for the Jason Leffler Memorial and finishes Saturday, Nov. 28, at Ventura Raceway with the 85th running of the ARP Turkey Night Grand Prix Presented by the West Coast Stock Car Hall of Fame.

text: The second Deuces Wild Championships runs Nov. 5-7 in Fort Worth, with two complete shows paying $5,000 and $7,000 to win and the POWRi 410 Outlaw Sprint League title on the line. The POWRi Honest Abe Roofing 410 Outlaw Sprint League wraps up its 2026 season this weekend at the…
body: The second Deuces Wild Championships runs Nov. 5-7 in Fort Worth, with two complete shows paying $5,000 and $7,000 to win and the POWRi 410 Outlaw Sprint League title on the line. The POWRi Honest Abe Roofing 410 Outlaw Sprint League wraps up its 2026 season this weekend at the Dirt Track at Texas Motor Speedway in Fort Worth, Texas, in the second running of the Deuces Wild Championships. The event also serves as the points finale for the POWRi Heartland Late Model Tour and the USRA American Racer Modified Series. New for 2026, time trials and hot laps for all three divisions move to Thursday, Nov. 5, with grandstands closed and racing beginning at 6:30 p.m. local time. Friday, Nov. 6 and Saturday, Nov. 7 are separate complete shows that go straight to heat races. Friday racing is set for 7 p.m.; Saturday starts a half-hour earlier, with racing estimated at 6:30 p.m. The 410 winged sprint cars race for $5,000 to win and $500 to start on Friday, and $7,000 to win and $500 to start on Saturday. Late Models pay $3,000 to win nightly and Modifieds $2,000, with about $110,000 in total purses across the weekend. The expected 410 field listed by event organizers includes Ryder McCutcheon (R), Joe B. Miller, Xavier Doney, Ayrton Gennetten, Landon Crawley, Gage Montgomery, Miles Paulus, Dylan Bloomfield, John Barnard, Scotty Milan, Natalie Doney, Kyle Bellm, Howard Moore, Roger Crockett, Joel Myers Jr., Blake Hahn, Jace Park, Colton Fisher (R), Kyle Clark, Jack Potter, Kaleb Johnson, Cam Sorrels, Kameron Key, Austin McCarl, Sam Hafertepe Jr., Justin Henderson, Austin Mundie, Weston Gorham, Ryan Padgett, Brenham Crouch, Rees Moran, Landon Thompson and Eric Baldaccini. Driver registration is free, and 120 paved pit spaces will be assigned first-come, first-served on Thursday. The National Weather Service forecast at the time of the event release called for sunny, dry conditions with highs in the 70s each day. A two-day adult grandstand pass is $53.98, and fan parking in the paved lot at the dirt track entrance is free. Start2Finish (S2FTV) will stream the event live. DirtSprintCars.com will post results after each night.

title: Rees Moran to Run Full-Time World of Outlaws Rookie Campaign With Greg Wheeler Motorsports in 2027
text: The 19-year-old from Tulsa, Oklahoma, is the first announced rookie contender for the 2027 Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year award. World of Outlaws said the team’s first season on the tour was split between Scotty Thiel and Skylar Gee in the No. 16C. Rees Moran will run a…
body: The 19-year-old from Tulsa, Oklahoma, is the first announced rookie contender for the 2027 Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year award. World of Outlaws said the team’s first season on the tour was split between Scotty Thiel and Skylar Gee in the No. 16C. Rees Moran will run a full-time rookie campaign with Greg Wheeler Motorsports in the World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series in 2027, the series announced Nov. 17. The 19-year-old from Tulsa, Oklahoma, is the first announced rookie contender for the 2027 Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year presented by Five Star Bodies award, according to World of Outlaws. Wheeler’s team completed its first World of Outlaws season in 2026, with Scotty Thiel driving through late April before Skylar Gee took over the No. 16C and finished the year, World of Outlaws said. Moran said he first met Wheeler during a rainout this year. “I actually met Greg, I think, during a rainout, and I was just walking around, and he was there, so I went and talked to him,” Moran said. “Greg’s a really great dude, and I’m really looking forward to it. He’s one of the nicest guys in the pit area, so to have someone like him wanting me to drive his race car is pretty surreal.” Moran spent much of 2026 in a 410 sprint car, World of Outlaws said. He drove Johnny Herrera’s No. 45X through the Knoxville Nationals, won a local feature at Huset’s Speedway and recorded four World of Outlaws top-10 finishes, three of them at I-55 Federated Auto Parts Raceway Park. He closed the year in his own No. 22M and won a POWRi race at Texas Motor Speedway Dirt Track. “It was my first year running for another car, so that was a little bit of a learning curve for me,” Moran said. “I’ve always just ran my family car.” He said winning in Herrera’s car and then in the family car to close the season “definitely does a bunch for my confidence going into next season.” His rookie World of Outlaws campaign begins Feb. 10-13 at Volusia Speedway Park’s Federated Auto Parts DIRTcar Nationals in Barberville, Florida, according to the series.

title: Ryan Newton Wins Australian Sprintcar Championship at Toowoomba
text: Newton passed Lachlan McHugh in the closing laps of the 40-lap A Main at Hi-Tec Oils Toowoomba Speedway on Saturday to win his first Australian 410 title. Brock Hallett finished second and McHugh third. Ryan Newton won the 64th Nutrend Homes Australian Sprintcar Championship on…
body: Newton passed Lachlan McHugh in the closing laps of the 40-lap A Main at Hi-Tec Oils Toowoomba Speedway on Saturday to win his first Australian 410 title. Brock Hallett finished second and McHugh third. Ryan Newton won the 64th Nutrend Homes Australian Sprintcar Championship on Saturday, Nov. 21, at Hi-Tec Oils Toowoomba Speedway in Toowoomba, Queensland, according to Speedcafe. Newton, driving the Q66, beat Brock Hallett (Q5) by 1.974 seconds in the 40-lap A Main, according to the event’s Race Monitor timing and scoring. Lachlan McHugh (NQ7) finished third, Brendan Quinn (S37) fourth and reigning champion Jock Goodyer (A1) fifth. Speedcafe reported it was Newton’s first Australian 410 Sprintcar title and that he became the first driver to hold the 410 and LS/360 Australian titles at the same time. Newton had a difficult qualifying session on Night 1 and had to race through a heat on Night 2, where he finished second to Goodyer, Speedcafe said. That put him into the Mid Pack Dash on points. He finished second there to transfer to the Stars Dash, which set the first four rows of the A Main, and finished third in the Stars Dash behind McHugh and Night 1 winner James McFadden. McHugh and McFadden swapped the lead on the opening lap, according to Speedcafe. McFadden’s title bid ended with 27 laps remaining when contact with a lapped car deflated his right-rear tire. With 15 laps to go, McHugh made contact with the lapped car of Randy Morgan on the back straight, but both continued. One lap later the race was stopped when Matthew Dumesny hit the wall and went onto his side after Goodyer moved across his nose entering turn 3. Luke Oldfield, who had been racing in the top five, pulled into the infield with a flat right-rear tire during the caution. McHugh pulled away again on the restart, but Newton caught him inside the final 10 laps, and the two swapped sides of the track for several laps, Speedcafe reported. McHugh drifted into the cushion in two straight corners inside the final five laps, letting Newton clear him. Hallett took second from McHugh with two laps to go. McHugh had led more than three quarters of the race. Goodyer won the second B Main and started 16th in the A Main before finishing fifth. Aaron Kelly (Q7) was sixth, Daniel Sayre (N16) seventh, Max Guilford (N79) eighth, Marcus Dumesny (N47) ninth and Morgan (Q54) 10th. “It’s unbelievable, I’ve got so many people to thank,” Newton told Speedcafe. “We’ve been working super hard, me and Damon, it’s finally paid off.” Speedcafe reported that it was the first time Toowoomba had hosted the championship, in the speedway’s 50th year of operation.

title: Ryan Timms Honored as Knoxville 410 Champion as 2027 Title Prize Doubles to $40,000
text: Timms was honored as a first-time champion at the 71st Knoxville Raceway awards banquet on Saturday, Nov. 21. Knoxville Raceway announced that the 2027 410 champion will receive $40,000, up from $20,000. Ryan Timms was honored as the 2026 Knoxville Championship Series champion…
body: Timms was honored as a first-time champion at the 71st Knoxville Raceway awards banquet on Saturday, Nov. 21. Knoxville Raceway announced that the 2027 410 champion will receive $40,000, up from $20,000. Ryan Timms was honored as the 2026 Knoxville Championship Series champion in the 410 sprint car class, his first title in the division, at the 71st Knoxville Raceway awards banquet on Saturday, Nov. 21, at Prairie Meadows Racetrack and Casino in Altoona, Iowa, according to a banquet report by Bill Wright published by SPEED SPORT and TJSlideways. Austin McCarl finished second in the 410 standings, Justin Henderson third, JJ Hickle fourth and Brian Brown fifth. Knoxville Raceway announced at the banquet that the 2027 Knoxville Championship Series point fund for the Leighton State Bank 410s will increase by $48,000, according to the report. The 2027 champion will receive $40,000, up from $20,000 in 2026, which KNIA-KRLS also reported. The 2027 fund pays $20,000 for second, $15,000 for third, $12,000 for fourth, $10,000 for fifth and $2,000 each for 15th through 20th. The report said more than $300,000 in cash and contingencies was handed out at the banquet, and the Knoxville Raceway Charitable Organization announced a $2,000 benefit for each of the 58 drivers who were point eligible in 2026. Tasker Phillips was honored as the 360 champion for the second time, according to the report, with Kade Higday second, Clint Garner third, Cam Martin fourth and Sawyer Phillips fifth. JJ Hickle won the 360 owner points. J Kinder won the Pro Sprint title, his third career championship, ahead of Tyler Thompson, Chase Young, Mike Mayberry and Casey Friedrichsen. Rookie of the Year honors went to Rees Moran in the 410 class, Evan Semerad in the 360 class and Matthew Botts in the Pro Sprints, according to SPEED SPORT, TJSlideways and KNIA-KRLS. Timms also received the 410 Lyle Boyd Hard Charger Award and the 410 feature lap leader award, and Brian Brown received the 410 Hoosier Tire Quick Time Award. Longtime race director John McCoy, who is retiring from that role, received the Ralph Capitani Heritage Award from National Sprint Car Hall of Fame & Museum executive director Bob Baker.

title: Ryder McCutcheon Wins 2026 POWRi 410 Outlaw Sprint League Championship
text: The Alamogordo, New Mexico, rookie took the title and Rookie of the Year honors with Huband Motorsports and RyderMac Racing, finishing 100 points ahead of Joe B. Miller. Ryder McCutcheon won the 2026 POWRi Honest Abe Roofing 410 Outlaw Sprint League championship as a rookie,…
body: The Alamogordo, New Mexico, rookie took the title and Rookie of the Year honors with Huband Motorsports and RyderMac Racing, finishing 100 points ahead of Joe B. Miller. Ryder McCutcheon won the 2026 POWRi Honest Abe Roofing 410 Outlaw Sprint League championship as a rookie, POWRi announced. The Alamogordo, New Mexico, driver also earned the league’s Rookie of the Year award in his first full season of 410 sprint car competition, driving for Huband Motorsports and RyderMac Racing. The title was decided at the season-ending Deuces Wild weekend at Texas Motor Speedway Dirt Track, which closed Saturday, Nov. 7. McCutcheon set quick time in Thursday qualifying and started second in the Championship Night feature, finishing eighth as Blake Hahn led all 25 laps for the win. Read the Texas finale story . In 24 feature starts, McCutcheon had two feature wins, two Quick Time awards, three heat race wins, one High Point Qualifier award, 64 laps led and a 7.7 average feature finish, according to POWRi. His first career POWRi 410 win came during the Road to the Hockett at Lucas Oil Speedway in June, and he won again at Humboldt Speedway on July 31. He also has a POWRi National Midget League feature win, giving him three career POWRi feature wins. POWRi’s final standings, released Nov. 11, show 140 points separating the top three. Joe B. Miller of Millersville, Missouri, finished second with 5,520 points, 100 behind McCutcheon, and Xavier Doney of Odessa, Missouri, was third with 5,480. Three-time champion Ayrton Gennetten finished fourth with 5,230 points, and Landon Crawley was fifth with 4,540 in the Beaver Special. The league drew 168 drivers across 28 completed events in 2026 despite seven rainouts, according to POWRi. Eleven drivers earned their first career league wins, including Jett Barnes, who became the youngest feature winner in series history at 15 years, three months and nine days with his Sept. 5 win at Lake Ozark Speedway.

title: Sam Hafertepe Jr. Wins Record Seventh ASCS National Tour Title
text: Hafertepe clinched the 2026 title Oct. 17 by winning the Fuzzy’s Fall Fling finale at Creek County Speedway with a last-lap pass. He beat Matt Covington by 41 points. After the season, he announced he will join Jess Jordan Motorsports in 2027 and shift his focus to selected 410…
body: Hafertepe clinched the 2026 title Oct. 17 by winning the Fuzzy’s Fall Fling finale at Creek County Speedway with a last-lap pass. He beat Matt Covington by 41 points. After the season, he announced he will join Jess Jordan Motorsports in 2027 and shift his focus to selected 410 World of Outlaws and High Limit starts. Sam Hafertepe Jr. of Sunnyvale, Texas, won the 2026 American Sprint Car Series National Tour championship, his seventh series title and the most in ASCS history. He clinched it Oct. 17 at Creek County Speedway in Sapulpa, Oklahoma, by winning the 40-lap Fuzzy’s Fall Fling season finale with a pass for the lead on the last lap, ASCS reported. Hafertepe entered the finale with a 21-point lead over Matt Covington and started eighth. He passed Covington for third with 14 laps left, got by Alex Sewell for second with two laps to go and took the lead from Garrett Benson in Turns 3 and 4 on the final lap. Benson finished second, Sewell third, Covington fourth and Steven Shebester fifth. Hafertepe won the title by 41 points over Covington. The win was Hafertepe’s seventh of 2026 and the 95th ASCS National Tour feature win of his career. He made 27 feature starts this season with 19 top-five and 21 top-10 finishes, according to ASCS season statistics. His first five titles came in consecutive seasons from 2016 to 2020, and his sixth, in 2025, moved him past Jason Johnson for the most in series history. Hafertepe and car owner Miles Hill won both the driver and owner championships with the Hill’s Racing Team No. 15H. “I owe it all to Miles and this team,” Hafertepe said at the ASCS awards banquet Oct. 18 in Tulsa. “For the last nine years, you’ve given us everything we need. This team never wavered this entire year, and as a driver, it’s the best kind of ownership you can have.” Covington finished second in points and Seth Bergman third. Hafertepe collected $40,000 from the series points fund. The 2027 ASCS National Tour season opens Feb. 4-6 at Volusia Speedway Park during the DIRTcar Nationals. After the season, a Jess Jordan Motorsports press release dated Oct. 20 said Hafertepe will join the newly formed, Texas-based team for 2027, concluding a partnership of nearly a decade with Hill’s Racing. The release said he will shift his focus from 360 to 410 sprint car racing and that his schedule will include selected World of Outlaws and High Limit events, with 2027 serving as a building year toward the long-term goal of competing on a national tour. Further details on the 2027 schedule will be announced later, the release said. Hafertepe posted the release on Oct. 21. Brody Brown, who was Hafertepe’s head mechanic this past season at 17 years old, will join him at Jess Jordan Motorsports, the release said. The partnership with Miles Hill and Hill’s Racing produced five ASCS National Tour championships and more than 80 feature victories, according to the release.

title: Giovanni Scelzi Serves Up Hot Sauce at Friday World Finals
text: Giovanni Scelzi led wire-to-wire after ripping past polesitter Sheldon Haudenschild on the opening lap to win Friday's 25-lap World of Outlaws feature at Charlotte. Tanner Holmes chased him home in second. Charlotte got a fresh dose of Hot Sauce on Friday night. Giovanni Scelzi,…
body: Giovanni Scelzi led wire-to-wire after ripping past polesitter Sheldon Haudenschild on the opening lap to win Friday's 25-lap World of Outlaws feature at Charlotte. Tanner Holmes chased him home in second. Charlotte got a fresh dose of Hot Sauce on Friday night. Giovanni Scelzi, in the Spire Motorsports Chili's No. 77, started on the front row and immediately made the move for the lead on the opening circuit, then never looked back in the 25-lap World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink feature at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. Tanner Holmes charged into second late and closed the gap in traffic, but ran out of laps as Scelzi took the checkered flag by 0.384 seconds. Sheldon Haudenschild, the polesitter, finished third. Cameron Smith and Buddy Schweibinz completed the top five. David Gravel, already the 2026 champion, was ninth. The win makes Scelzi the 24th different World of Outlaws winner in 2026, one shy of the record for most in a season with one night remaining. It's his 11th career WoO victory. Scelzi noted the cushion got lipped up after the till, but credited the track crew and fans who stuck around for nearly 12 hours. Winning in Spire's home state with the Chili's car was a nice bonus — seven years since his last Charlotte triumph. The World Finals wrap Saturday with the $25,000-to-win season finale. Hot Sauce is back on the menu.

title: Logan Seavey and Abacus Racing Part Ways
text: Logan Seavey has stepped away from his role with Abacus Racing, effective immediately, ending a four-year partnership. He said he has no plans in place for 2027. Logan Seavey announced Nov. 3 that he has made what he called a difficult decision to step away from his role with…
body: Logan Seavey has stepped away from his role with Abacus Racing, effective immediately, ending a four-year partnership. He said he has no plans in place for 2027. Logan Seavey announced Nov. 3 that he has made what he called a difficult decision to step away from his role with Abacus Racing, effective immediately, after four successful years together. In a statement released by Logan Seavey Racing, he said he is grateful for the opportunity to compete with the team and for everything they accomplished during their time together. Seavey thanked Brent, John, Ken, Kirk, Daniel, Johnny, Ronnie, Trevor, Chad and every partner who contributed to the team. He said the hard work and support from those people did not go unnoticed and is what contributed to the team’s success. Seavey said he does not have plans in place for 2027. He said he is looking forward to exploring his options and finding the right opportunity to continue competing at a high level next season. Seavey thanked everyone who has supported him over the years and said he will share more details once his plans for 2027 are finalized.

text: Sussex started seventh in the Jack Yeley-owned No. 2 and passed Charles Davis Jr. for the lead on lap 17 at Casa Grande, Ariz., on Saturday, Nov. 14. Stevie Sussex won the 25-lap USAC Avanti Windows & Doors Southwest Sprint Car feature at Central Arizona Raceway in Casa Grande,…
body: Sussex started seventh in the Jack Yeley-owned No. 2 and passed Charles Davis Jr. for the lead on lap 17 at Casa Grande, Ariz., on Saturday, Nov. 14. Stevie Sussex won the 25-lap USAC Avanti Windows & Doors Southwest Sprint Car feature at Central Arizona Raceway in Casa Grande, Arizona, on Saturday, Nov. 14, according to USAC. Davis, the series’ second all-time winningest driver, took the lead back on lap 7. Sussex passed him on lap 17 and led the final nine laps. Davis finished second, point leader R.J. St. James set fast time at 15.850 seconds, two-thousandths of a second ahead of La Rose, USAC said. Davis and Sussex won the two eight-lap heat races. Jonas Reynolds flipped in the first heat and Bryan Ledbetter Jr. flipped in the second heat, according to the official results. Johnson leads the USAC Southwest Sprint Car standings with 1,128 points, 217 ahead of Shelton (911). St. James is third with 842, Daylin Perreira fourth with 835 and Koen Crawford fifth with 811. title: Kody Swanson Wins Non-Winged Feature at Open Wheel Showdown
text: Kody Swanson added another Open Wheel Showdown victory, taking the $10,000 inaugural non-winged sprint car feature at the Bullring at Las Vegas Motor Speedway on Friday night. Kody Swanson continues to dominate the OnlyBulls Open Wheel Showdown. On Friday night at the Bullring…
body: Kody Swanson added another Open Wheel Showdown victory, taking the $10,000 inaugural non-winged sprint car feature at the Bullring at Las Vegas Motor Speedway on Friday night. Kody Swanson continues to dominate the OnlyBulls Open Wheel Showdown. On Friday night at the Bullring at Las Vegas Motor Speedway, Swanson won the inaugural Elliott’s Custom Trailers & Carts Non-Winged sprint car feature, leading the 75-lap race to the $10,000 prize. Swanson, who previously won the midget feature in 2023 and the winged sprint car features in 2024 and 2025, started near the front and took the lead early. He and Jackson Macenko traded the top spot in traffic before Swanson reclaimed control on the high side on Lap 42 and drove away to a 6.5-second victory. Evan Margeson finished second, with Chris Muhler third. The non-winged class drew a strong field of 59 cars for its debut at the event, highlighting the growing interest in pavement non-winged sprint car racing. title: Terry Gray to Make Final Starts at USCS Flip Flop 50 at Riverside
text: The 16-time United Sprint Car Series national champion and 2022 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame inductee says the series finale this weekend at Riverside International Speedway will be his last competition. Terry Gray of Bartlett, Tenn., a 16-time United Sprint Car Series…
body: The 16-time United Sprint Car Series national champion and 2022 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame inductee says the series finale this weekend at Riverside International Speedway will be his last competition. Terry Gray of Bartlett, Tenn., a 16-time United Sprint Car Series national champion and 2022 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame inductee, will compete Friday and Saturday at Riverside International Speedway in West Memphis, Ark., in what he says is his final competition after a 52-year sprint car career, according to a post Friday from the track. Gray is entered in the USCS season finale, the ACE DORAN Rigging & Hauling 18th Annual Bobby Martin Memorial USCS Flip Flop 50 presented by XC Gear, on Nov. 20 and 21. Gray leads the 2026 Hoosier Racing Tire USCS Outlaw Thunder Tour presented by XC Gear national standings with 3,080 points, 22 ahead of Jeff Willingham of Ripley, Miss., according to the series standings. He also leads the USCS MidSouth Thunder Tour. Preliminary events are scheduled Friday night, with twin 25-lap A-Mains on Saturday. The event has more than $10,000 on the line with bonuses, according to the track and a series preview by USCS founder and president Pete Walton. Gray earned his 99th career USCS feature win on Sept. 5 at Dixie Speedway in Woodstock, Ga., according to a USCS report, and the Riverside post said he comes into the weekend with 99 series wins. Besides his 16 national titles, the track said Gray has more than 50 USCS national and regional series titles on pavement and dirt. USCS reports have repeatedly identified him as a 16-time national champion. The National Sprint Car Hall of Fame inducted Gray in its class of 2022, noting a 1980 World of Outlaws win at Riverside, four consecutive American Sprint Car Series national championships from 1995 through 1998, and a USCS career that began in 2001. USCS founder and president Pete Walton said, according to the Riverside post, “Terry Gray has made not only a huge contribution to the United Sprint Car Series, but to the sport of sprint racing in general. He has been an iconic figure, especially in the winged-360 portion of the sport where his success on both dirt and paved ovals as well is unmatched. There are really not many Terry Grays left in this sport. He has made such a contribution to our series and to others as a driver, car owner, mentor, advisor and friend to many. We wish him all the very best in his next move, while not still behind the wheel of a race car. He will be missed as a competitor.”

title: Travis DeGaton Wins 2026 POWRi Southwest Ecotec Midget Championship
text: DeGaton won a series-leading seven features and took the title by 80 points over Shon Deskins, POWRi announced Nov. 17. Travis DeGaton of Sacramento, California, won the 2026 POWRi Avanti Windows & Doors Southwest Ecotec Midget Series championship, POWRi announced Nov. 17.…
body: DeGaton won a series-leading seven features and took the title by 80 points over Shon Deskins, POWRi announced Nov. 17. Travis DeGaton of Sacramento, California, won the 2026 POWRi Avanti Windows & Doors Southwest Ecotec Midget Series championship, POWRi announced Nov. 17. DeGaton won a series-leading seven features and finished 80 points ahead of Shon Deskins of Waddell, Arizona. Driving the No. 14X, DeGaton recorded 13 top-five finishes and 14 top-10 finishes in 17 feature starts, according to POWRi. His seven victories brought his career total in the series to 10, the most in series history. POWRi said he earned his first win of the season on May 9 at Adobe Mountain Speedway, won again on May 24 during Salute to Indy weekend after setting quick time and earning High Point Qualifier honors, started on the pole and led 16 of 20 laps at Deuce of Clubs Thunder Raceway in August for his sixth win, and closed the season with his seventh victory at Adobe Mountain. DeGaton finished with 4,730 points. Deskins was second with 4,650 points, one feature win, nine top-five finishes and 15 top-10 finishes in 17 starts. Grant Schaadt of San Tan Valley, Arizona, was third with 4,640 points, five feature wins and 15 top-five finishes in 16 starts, 10 points behind Deskins. POWRi said the top three drivers combined to win 13 of the season’s 18 features and finished within 90 points of one another. Gary DeWitt of Mesa, Arizona, was fourth with 4,080 points, one feature win, six top-fives and 14 top-10s. Tyler Ruth of Glendale, Arizona, was fifth with 4,030 points, seven top-fives and 13 top-10s in 16 starts.

body: The 71st annual banquet at the Indiana Roof Ballroom will honor USAC’s 2026 titlists and special award winners. Tickets are $75, and the RSVP deadline is Dec. 4. The United States Auto Club will hold its 71st annual Night of Champions on Friday, Dec. 11, at the Indiana Roof Ballroom in Indianapolis, USAC announced. The banquet will honor USAC’s 2026 champions and special award winners. A cocktail hour starts at 6 p.m. Eastern, with opening ceremonies at 6:30 p.m., followed by dinner and the awards, according to USAC Media’s Richie Murray. Tickets are $75 each and include the reception, dinner and two drinks, USAC said. Children’s tickets are $40. The RSVP deadline is Friday, Dec. 4, and USAC said prices will go up after that date. Tickets are sold through USAC’s online ticket page and will be available for pickup at the ballroom on the night of the banquet. The NASCAR Youth Series Quarter Midget awards banquet will be held earlier the same day, at 3 p.m. Eastern at the Indiana Roof Ballroom, with light food and drinks from 2 p.m., according to USAC. That event is free, but a quarter midget banquet ticket does not admit the holder to the Night of Champions. Each NASCAR Youth Series champion will receive one champion banner, and extra banners cost $25, USAC said. USAC has already named several 2026 champions in its season reviews. Kyle Cummins won the AMSOIL National Sprint Car title, Steven Drevicki the East Coast Sprint Car title, Jack Wagner the MRA Sprint Car title, R.J. Johnson the CRA Sprint Car title, Tyler Nelson the Midwest Thunder SpeeD2 Midget title and Broedy Graham the Western States Midget title. The NOS Energy Drink National Midget title is still open. Five races remain, starting Nov. 18 at Plaza Park Raceway in Visalia, California (that date was rescheduled for Monday, Nov. 23, according to USAC Media, Nov. 17 ; read the update ), and Jacob Denney leads Kevin Thomas Jr. by 73 points, according to USAC.

title: Jack Wagner Wins 2026 USAC Wholesale Batteries MRA Sprint Car Title
text: Driving the Jesse Hockett/Wagner Boys Racing No. 77, Wagner won seven of 12 series starts and finished 125 points ahead of Chase Howard. Jack Wagner of Lone Jack, Missouri won the 2026 USAC Wholesale Batteries Midwest Racing Association Sprint Car championship. In the Jesse…
body: Driving the Jesse Hockett/Wagner Boys Racing No. 77, Wagner won seven of 12 series starts and finished 125 points ahead of Chase Howard. Jack Wagner of Lone Jack, Missouri won the 2026 USAC Wholesale Batteries Midwest Racing Association Sprint Car championship. In the Jesse Hockett/Wagner Boys Racing No. 77, known as “The Crow,” Wagner posted seven victories, four second-place finishes and a fifth in 12 series starts and defeated Chase Howard of Nesbit, Mississippi by 125 points, 1,769-1,654. Wagner also led the series with 172 laps led, six heat-race wins, and top-five and top-10 finishes in all 12 of his starts. He won three times at Grain Valley, Missouri’s Valley Speedway, in June, August and October’s John Helm Memorial, added a pair of victories at Butler, Missouri’s Electric City Speedway in May and July, and also won in July at Kansas City, Kansas’ Lakeside Speedway and Winston, Missouri’s I-35 Speedway. USAC noted it was his best season driving a non-winged sprint car. He won more races across all divisions in 2026 (10) than he had in the previous five seasons combined (8). Ricky Lewis won two of his three series starts, including April’s season opener at Springfield Raceway on a last-lap pass of Braydon Cromwell. Wyatt Burks passed Wagner with two laps remaining to win August’s Weld Memorial at Lakeside. Tom Curran collected his first career sprint car win after passing Wagner in June at Valley, and Wesley Smith passed Wagner with two laps remaining to win in May at Valley. Burks finished third in the standings, just ahead of Wagner’s brother, Samuel Wagner, with Cromwell fifth. Ten drivers started all 12 points-paying features, including both Wagners, Howard, Burks and Cromwell.
