title: World of Outlaws Set Eight 2027 Pennsylvania Dates, Opening May 12 at Lincoln
text: The series will face the PA Posse in eight races at Lincoln Speedway, Williams Grove Speedway and BAPS Motor Speedway, from the Gettysburg Clash on May 12 to the 65th National Open on Oct. 1-2. The World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series will race eight times in…
body: The series will face the PA Posse in eight races at Lincoln Speedway, Williams Grove Speedway and BAPS Motor Speedway, from the Gettysburg Clash on May 12 to the 65th National Open on Oct. 1-2. The World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series will race eight times in Pennsylvania in 2027, the series announced Nov. 12. The dates are spread over three tracks: Lincoln Speedway, Williams Grove Speedway in Mechanicsburg and BAPS Motor Speedway in York Haven. According to World of Outlaws, the series won five of the eight Pennsylvania races against the PA Posse in 2026, and Posse drivers won three. The swing opens Wednesday, May 12, with the Gettysburg Clash at Lincoln Speedway. Buddy Kofoid and Roth Motorsports have won the last two runnings of the race, the series said. The series then moves to Williams Grove for the HVAC Distributors Morgan Cup on Friday and Saturday, May 14-15. In 2026, Kasey Kahne won the Morgan Cup opener for his first World of Outlaws win, and David Gravel won the finale, according to World of Outlaws. Three summer races follow. The Bricker’s Bash is set for Thursday, July 29, at BAPS Motor Speedway, where Chase Dietz won for the Posse in 2026. Williams Grove then hosts the C&D Rigging Summer Nationals on July 30-31. Kofoid and Gravel won the two 2026 Summer Nationals races, the series said. The Pennsylvania schedule ends with the 65th J&S Classics National Open at Williams Grove on Friday and Saturday, Oct. 1-2. In 2026, Gravel won the opening night and Dietz won the National Open title and $75,000, according to World of Outlaws. The series said ticket information for the Pennsylvania races will be announced later. The 2027 World of Outlaws season begins Feb. 10-13 with the Federated Auto Parts DIRTcar Nationals at Volusia Speedway Park in Barberville, Florida, according to the series.

title: Gravel Honored for Third Straight Title, Kyle Ripper Earns Two Awards at World of Outlaws Banquet
text: Kyle Ripper was named Crew Chief of the Year and received the NOS Energy Drink Eloy Gutierrez Spirit Award. Sheldon Haudenschild was voted Most Popular Driver, and Emerson Axsom was named Rookie of the Year. Kyle Ripper received two honors Sunday night, Nov. 8, at the 2026 World…
body: Kyle Ripper was named Crew Chief of the Year and received the NOS Energy Drink Eloy Gutierrez Spirit Award. Sheldon Haudenschild was voted Most Popular Driver, and Emerson Axsom was named Rookie of the Year. Kyle Ripper received two honors Sunday night, Nov. 8, at the 2026 World of Outlaws Awards Celebration in Charlotte, N.C., the night after the World Finals closed the World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series season. Ripper, crew chief for Sheldon Haudenschild on the KCP Racing entry, was named the series’ Crew Chief of the Year and also received the NOS Energy Drink Eloy Gutierrez Spirit Award , according to the World of Outlaws. The series described Ripper as Haudenschild’s longtime crew chief and said he “continues to be entirely dedicated to Sprint Car Racing and the World of Outlaws.” Haudenschild was named the 2026 World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Most Popular Driver , an award decided by fan voting, according to the series. Emerson Axsom received the Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year award presented by Five Star Bodies. Axsom opened 2026 by winning the Chili Bowl Nationals and earned his first World of Outlaws feature win Sept. 6 at Huset’s Speedway in the Klaasmeyer/Petry Motorsports No. 27. Series statistics credit him with one win, 11 top-five finishes and 32 top-10s in 70 feature starts this season. Announcer Johnny Gibson received the Ted Johnson Award after his 30th season calling World of Outlaws Sprint Car races. “I’m the luckiest Sprint Car fan in the world,” Gibson said in a video posted by the series. Ace Pruitt of Stenhouse Jr./Marshall Racing was named the Jason Johnson Sportsman of the Year . Brian Morrison was again named Engine Builder of the Year ; the series noted that Morrison Racing Engines powers Big Game Motorsports and KCP Racing, the teams that finished first and third in the 2026 standings. The banquet followed David Gravel’s official crowning Saturday night at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. Gravel won his third consecutive World of Outlaws championship with Big Game Motorsports, finishing the season with 11 wins, 48 top-five finishes and 66 top-10s in 75 starts, according to the series. He joins Steve Kinser, Donny Schatz and Brad Sweet as the only drivers to win at least three straight series titles. The 2027 season opens Feb. 10-13 at Volusia Speedway Park.

title: Steve Kinser “The King”
text: World of Outlaws. Steve Kinser is the winningest driver in World of Outlaws history, with 20 WoO championships and 690 feature wins. "The King" won the inaugural 1978 Outlaws title, a record 12 Knoxville Nationals and seven Kings Royals. Steve Kinser built the World of Outlaws…
body: Steve Kinser is the winningest driver in World of Outlaws history, with 20 WoO championships and 690 feature wins. "The King" won the inaugural 1978 Outlaws title, a record 12 Knoxville Nationals and seven Kings Royals. Steve Kinser built the World of Outlaws into a national institution as much as any promoter did. Arriving for the series' first season in 1978, the Bloomington, Indiana, driver and his cousin Karl Kinser's team set the standard every touring sprint car program has chased since, and the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame later named him sprint car racing's greatest driver of the century. He won the inaugural 1978 Outlaws title and 20 series championships in all. His 690 World of Outlaws A-feature wins are nearly 300 more than anyone else, a margin unmatched in American motorsports. Kinser owned the sport's crown jewels. He won the Knoxville Nationals a record 12 times and the Kings Royal at Eldora seven times, the National Open at Williams Grove four times (1990, 1992, 1994 and 2003), and among the majors he won the Gold Cup Race of Champions at Chico more than ten times. His 1987 season remains the benchmark. He won 46 Outlaws features that year, including 24 of the final 26. Kinser was versatile beyond the dirt. He won the 1994 IROC race at Talladega, started the 1995 Daytona 500 and drove in the 1997 Indianapolis 500. He briefly left the Outlaws for the National Sprint Tour in 2006, returned in 2007, and retired from sprint car racing in 2016. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2005 and the Motorsports Hall of Fame of America in 2017. His son Kraig, himself a 2005 Knoxville Nationals winner, carried the family name forward. 20 World of Outlaws championships 690 World of Outlaws feature wins (all-time record) Won the inaugural 1978 WoO title 4 Williams Grove National Open wins (1990, 1992, 1994, 2003) 20 WoO titles 690 WoO wins Crown jewels: 12 Knoxville Nationals, 7 Kings Royals, 4 National Opens Steve Kinser at Knoxville Raceway, Aug. 11, 2004.

title: Sammy Swindell “Slammin' Sammy”
text: World of Outlaws. Sammy Swindell is a three-time World of Outlaws champion (1981, 1982, 1997) whose 394 WoO feature wins rank second all-time. He also won the 1983 Knoxville Nationals, three Kings Royals and five Chili Bowl Midget Nationals, and in 1997 he became the first…
body: Sammy Swindell is a three-time World of Outlaws champion (1981, 1982, 1997) whose 394 WoO feature wins rank second all-time. He also won the 1983 Knoxville Nationals, three Kings Royals and five Chili Bowl Midget Nationals, and in 1997 he became the first owner-driver to win the Outlaws title. Sammy Swindell was the engineer of the modern sprint car as much as its driver. A technically minded Tennessean from a racing family, he was one of the Memphis-area group that helped make the early World of Outlaws, and alongside Steve Kinser and Doug Wolfgang he is remembered as one of the "Big Three" of winged sprint car racing. He won Outlaws championships in 1981 and 1982. In 1997 he won a third title in his own car, becoming the first owner-driver to win the WoO crown. He was also runner-up four times, and his 394 World of Outlaws A-main wins rank second all-time. Swindell won the 1983 Knoxville Nationals and the Kings Royal in 1992, 1999 and 2012. In 1981 he took the wing off to win the Pacific Coast Nationals at Ascot. In midgets he won the Chili Bowl five times: 1989, 1992, 1996, 1998 and 2009. Swindell also tested himself elsewhere. He made CART starts in 1985 and 1986, failed to qualify for the 1987 Indianapolis 500, and ran the inaugural 1995 NASCAR Truck Series season, finishing 12th in points. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2006. 3 World of Outlaws championships 394 WoO feature wins (2nd all-time) 4-time WoO championship runner-up 2 Williams Grove National Open wins (1997, 2010) 3 WoO titles 394 WoO wins Crown jewels: 1 Knoxville Nationals, 3 Kings Royals, 2 National Opens 5 Chili Bowls Sammy Swindell at Knoxville Raceway, August 1997.

title: Donny Schatz
text: World of Outlaws. Donny Schatz is a ten-time World of Outlaws champion, second only to Steve Kinser, and an 11-time Knoxville Nationals winner. Driving for Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing from 2008, he also won six Kings Royals and a record six Williams Grove National Opens.…
body: Donny Schatz is a ten-time World of Outlaws champion, second only to Steve Kinser, and an 11-time Knoxville Nationals winner. Driving for Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing from 2008, he also won six Kings Royals and a record six Williams Grove National Opens. Donny Schatz built the most sustained championship program of the World of Outlaws' modern era. The Fargo, North Dakota, driver was the series' 1997 Rookie of the Year, won his first Outlaws feature in 1998, and joined Tony Stewart's team in 2008. That partnership with Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing ran 18 seasons and produced most of his titles. Schatz won ten World of Outlaws championships: 2006 through 2009, 2012, and 2014 through 2018. Only Steve Kinser has won more. He has 318 Outlaws feature wins, which rank third all-time behind Steve Kinser and Sammy Swindell. He won the Knoxville Nationals 11 times, in 2006–09, 2011–15, 2017 and 2022, one short of Kinser's record. He also won six Kings Royals and a record six National Opens at Williams Grove. Fans know him for his consistency across a full season and his command of sprint car racing's crown-jewel events. 10 World of Outlaws championships 318 WoO feature wins (3rd all-time) 11-time Knoxville Nationals champion 6 Kings Royal and 6 National Open wins 1997 WoO Rookie of the Year 2 Grand Annual Sprintcar Classic wins at Warrnambool, Australia (2001, 2002) 10 WoO titles 318 WoO wins Crown jewels: 11 Knoxville Nationals, 6 Kings Royals, 6 National Opens, 2 Australian Classics Donny Schatz in his Tony Stewart Racing firesuit, 2025 World of Outlaws portrait.

body: Mark Kinser won World of Outlaws titles in 1996 and 1999, and his 203 series wins rank fourth all-time. He also won the Knoxville Nationals three times. Mark Kinser of Oolitic, Indiana, is a cousin of Steve Kinser. He was World of Outlaws co-Rookie of the Year in 1984 and ran his own team for a decade before joining his father, Karl Kinser, in 1995. He won World of Outlaws championships in 1996 and 1999 and was runner-up in 1991, 1998 and 2001. His 203 World of Outlaws wins rank fourth all-time. He won the Knoxville Nationals in 1996, 1999 and 2000 and the 2001 Kings Royal at Eldora. title: Doug Wolfgang
text: World of Outlaws. Doug Wolfgang of Sioux Falls, South Dakota, is a five-time Knoxville Nationals champion with 140 World of Outlaws feature wins, fifth-most all-time. He was one of the "Big Three" of the early Outlaws era, and he also won two Kings Royals and 37 All Star Circuit…
body: Doug Wolfgang of Sioux Falls, South Dakota, is a five-time Knoxville Nationals champion with 140 World of Outlaws feature wins, fifth-most all-time. He was one of the "Big Three" of the early Outlaws era, and he also won two Kings Royals and 37 All Star Circuit of Champions races. Doug Wolfgang carried the Midwest's homegrown sprint car scene onto the national stage. The Sioux Falls, South Dakota, driver came up in super modifieds and, with car owner Bob Trostle, broke through at Knoxville in the mid-1970s before becoming one of the "Big Three" of the early World of Outlaws era. Wolfgang won the Knoxville Nationals five times, in 1977, 1978, 1984, 1985 and 1989. He won them for four different owners: Trostle, Bill Smith, Bob Weikert and Danny Peace. With the Outlaws he finished second in the standings four times and won 140 features, fifth-most in series history. He also won 37 All Star Circuit of Champions races and two Kings Royals. On April 3, 1992, a fiery crash at Lakeside Speedway in Kansas City left him with burns over about 30 percent of his body and a broken vertebra. He came back to win an IMCA 360 sprint championship and the 1996 ASCS 360 Nationals, then retired in 1997 after another serious crash. Wolfgang is a member of the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame and later built sprint car chassis from his shop near Sioux Falls. 140 World of Outlaws wins (5th all-time) 5-time Knoxville Nationals champion 2-time Kings Royal winner 37 All Star Circuit of Champions wins 3 straight Williams Grove National Open wins (1984, 1985, 1986) for Bob Weikert 140 WoO wins 37 All Star wins Crown jewels: 5 Knoxville Nationals, 2 Kings Royals, 3 National Opens Doug Wolfgang driving the Weikert's Livestock No. 29 sprint car.

title: Rico Abreu
text: High Limit Racing. Rico Abreu won consecutive High Limit Racing championships in 2025 and 2026, with eight High Limit wins in 2026. He is the series' all-time leader in wins, starts, podiums and top-10 finishes. He also won the 2014 USAC National Midget championship and…
body: Rico Abreu won consecutive High Limit Racing championships in 2025 and 2026, with eight High Limit wins in 2026. He is the series' all-time leader in wins, starts, podiums and top-10 finishes. He also won the 2014 USAC National Midget championship and back-to-back Chili Bowl Midget Nationals in 2015 and 2016. Rico Abreu has been part of High Limit Racing from its start and helped build it into a national tour. Abreu is a Northern Californian who has achondroplasia and is four feet four inches tall. He has run every High Limit points race since 2023 and holds the series' career records for wins, starts, podiums and top-10 finishes. He made his name in midgets. He won the 2014 USAC National Midget championship, then won the Chili Bowl Midget Nationals in back-to-back years, 2015 and 2016. Stock cars came next, with backing from his friend Kyle Larson. He won the 2015 NASCAR K&N Pro Series East race at Columbus Motor Speedway, his first stock car win, before returning to open-wheel racing. Back on dirt, he became a regular winner at marquee events, including the Outlaws and High Limit shows at Eldora's 4-Crown. He won his first national sprint car championship, the 2025 High Limit title, by winning the season finale at Texas Motor Speedway. He retained the High Limit championship in 2026 with Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing, winning eight High Limit features that season. 2025 and 2026 High Limit Racing champion Eight High Limit wins in 2026 All-time High Limit wins leader 2014 USAC National Midget champion 2 High Limit titles (2025–26) 8 High Limit wins in 2026 2014 USAC Midget title 2 Chili Bowls Rico Abreu, World of Outlaws.

title: Kyle Larson “Yung Money”
text: High Limit Racing. Kyle Larson co-founded High Limit Racing, won its first championship and put together the 2020 dirt season people still measure everything against: 46 wins in 97 starts. He is a three-time NASCAR Cup Series champion (2021, 2025 and 2026), a 2015 Rolex 24 at…
body: Kyle Larson co-founded High Limit Racing, won its first championship and put together the 2020 dirt season people still measure everything against: 46 wins in 97 starts. He is a three-time NASCAR Cup Series champion (2021, 2025 and 2026), a 2015 Rolex 24 at Daytona winner, and a winner of the Coca-Cola 600 and the Brickyard 400. Kyle Larson of Elk Grove, California, came up through California micros and midgets before NASCAR came calling. He never left dirt behind. In 2020, with NASCAR on hold for him, he raced dirt almost every night and won 46 of 97 starts in sprint cars, midgets, Silver Crown and a dirt late model. That is a .474 winning percentage against the best drivers in the sport. Running only 26 of the 54 World of Outlaws events, he still led the series with 12 wins. He also won his first Chili Bowl that year, swept Indiana Midget Week, and won the Hoosier Hundred and the Bettenhausen 100 on the dirt miles. With Brad Sweet he announced High Limit Racing at Eldora in July 2022. He won the series' inaugural championship in 2023, and in late 2023 High Limit took over the All Star Circuit of Champions from Tony Stewart. Through the 2026 national season he had 15 High Limit wins. His dirt crown jewels include three Chili Bowls (2020, 2021, 2025), four Knoxville Nationals (2021, 2023, 2024, 2026) and the 2021 Kings Royal. In NASCAR he won the Cup Series championship with Hendrick Motorsports in 2021, with 10 wins, again in 2025, and a third time in 2026 at Homestead-Miami Speedway, becoming a back-to-back champion. He also won the 2021 Coca-Cola 600 and the 2024 Brickyard 400, and in sports cars he won the 2015 Rolex 24 at Daytona with Jamie McMurray and Chip Ganassi Racing. He was named one of NASCAR's 75 Greatest Drivers. 2023 High Limit Racing champion (inaugural season) High Limit Racing co-founder (2022) 2020: 46 wins in 97 dirt starts; 12 World of Outlaws wins, most in the series Chili Bowl: 2020, 2021, 2025 Knoxville Nationals: 2021, 2023, 2024, 2026 NASCAR Cup Series champion: 2021, 2025, 2026 (back-to-back in 2025–26) 2021 Coca-Cola 600 winner; 2024 Brickyard 400 winner 2015 Rolex 24 at Daytona winner (with Jamie McMurray, Chip Ganassi Racing) 2023 High Limit title 15 High Limit wins (through 2026) 3 NASCAR Cup titles (2021, 2025, 2026) 2020: 46 wins in 97 starts 3 Chili Bowls 4 Knoxville Nationals 2021 Coca-Cola 600; 2024 Brickyard 400 2015 Rolex 24 at Daytona Kyle Larson in Casey's Victory Lane at the Knoxville Nationals, 2025.

title: Jack Hewitt
text: All Star Circuit of Champions. Jack Hewitt of Troy, Ohio, won the 1985 All Star Circuit of Champions title and ranks fifth all-time in All Stars feature wins. Blunt and outspoken, he never minced words, and that made him one of the biggest fan favorites in Midwestern dirt…
body: Jack Hewitt of Troy, Ohio, won the 1985 All Star Circuit of Champions title and ranks fifth all-time in All Stars feature wins. Blunt and outspoken, he never minced words, and that made him one of the biggest fan favorites in Midwestern dirt racing. Jack Hewitt of Troy, Ohio, was the people's hero of Midwestern dirt racing. He was a racer's racer who would run anything, anywhere, and he was the son of racer Don Hewitt. He was a fan favorite as much for his personality as his driving. Blunt and outspoken, he never minced words, and fans loved him for it. He won the 1985 All Star Circuit of Champions title with 12 wins that year, and his 55 All Stars feature wins rank fifth all-time. He also won 46 USAC National Sprint Car features and Silver Crown titles in 1986 and 1987. In 1998 he reached the Indianapolis 500 and finished 12th. That same year he swept all four features at Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals, in Silver Crown, Sprint, Midget and modified, for four different teams. In all he has won 19 4-Crown features, the most of anyone. He is a member of the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (2002) and the USAC Hall of Fame. 46 USAC National Sprint Car wins National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (2002) 2-time USAC Silver Crown champion 1985 All Star Circuit of Champions champion Only driver to sweep all four features at Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals (1998) 1985 All Stars champion 55 All Stars wins (5th) 46 USAC Sprint wins Jack Hewitt in a USAC sprint car at Winchester, April 2, 1995.

title: Pancho Carter
text: USAC Sprint Cars. Pancho Carter was USAC's first career Triple Crown champion. He won the 1972 National Midget title, the 1974 and 1976 Sprint Car titles and the 1978 Silver Crown title. He also made 17 Indianapolis 500 starts, won the 1985 Indy pole and won the 1981 Michigan…
body: Pancho Carter was USAC's first career Triple Crown champion. He won the 1972 National Midget title, the 1974 and 1976 Sprint Car titles and the 1978 Silver Crown title. He also made 17 Indianapolis 500 starts, won the 1985 Indy pole and won the 1981 Michigan 500. Pancho Carter set the template for USAC versatility. The son of USAC Hall of Famer Duane Carter, he became the organization's first career Triple Crown champion and showed a generation of short-track drivers that one racer could master midgets, sprints and Silver Crown cars. He won the 1972 USAC National Midget title and Sprint Car titles in 1974 and 1976. In 1978 he won the Silver Crown title, then called the USAC National Dirt Championship. He scored 70 USAC national feature wins across those series. Carter was the 1974 Indianapolis 500 Rookie of the Year and made 17 Indy 500 starts. He won the pole in 1985 and finished third in 1982. He also won the 1981 Michigan 500. He is a member of both the National Sprint Car and National Midget Halls of Fame and the USAC Hall of Fame. First USAC Triple Crown champion 1974 & 1976 USAC Sprint champion 4 USAC titles (Midget, 2 Sprint, Silver Crown) 70 USAC national wins Triple Crown Pancho Carter, USAC.

title: Dave Darland “The People's Champ”
text: USAC Sprint Cars. Dave Darland, the "People's Champ," is a USAC Triple Crown champion with titles in Silver Crown (1997), Sprint (1999) and Midget (2001–02). He retired in 2023 with 62 USAC National Sprint Car wins, then the record, and a record 20 Indiana Sprint Week wins. Dave…
body: Dave Darland, the "People's Champ," is a USAC Triple Crown champion with titles in Silver Crown (1997), Sprint (1999) and Midget (2001–02). He retired in 2023 with 62 USAC National Sprint Car wins, then the record, and a record 20 Indiana Sprint Week wins. Dave Darland was USAC's everyman champion. Fans called him the "People's Champ." Over nearly four decades he made more USAC national starts than anyone, 1,334, and he showed that a local Indiana sprint car racer could become one of the sport's all-time greats. Born in 1966 in Lincoln, Indiana, he won four national titles: Silver Crown in 1997, Sprint in 1999, and Midget in 2001 and 2002. That made him the third career Triple Crown champion. His 62 USAC National Sprint Car wins were the record when he retired in 2023. His 20 Indiana Sprint Week wins are still the most of any driver. He won 115 USAC features nationally and regionally, including 30 National Midget and 14 Silver Crown wins. He won at least one USAC national feature in a record 24 straight seasons, 1993 through 2016. Along the way he won Turkey Night, the midget classic, twice. Darland is a member of the USAC Hall of Fame. body: Tom Bigelow was the 1978 USAC National Sprint Car champion, and his 52 series wins were the all-time record for more than 30 years. Tom Bigelow, a Wisconsin native who made his home in Winchester, Indiana, won the 1978 USAC National Sprint Car championship. His 52 USAC National Sprint Car wins stood as the series record from 1981 until Dave Darland passed him in 2014, and they still rank fourth all-time. He also ranks first in series history in fast-qualifier awards. title: Tracy Hines
text: USAC Sprint Cars. Tracy Hines is a USAC Triple Crown champion with Silver Crown (2000), Sprint (2002) and Midget (2015) titles. He won 91 USAC national races, including 47 in sprint cars, and he won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons. Tracy Hines spent most of…
body: Tracy Hines is a USAC Triple Crown champion with Silver Crown (2000), Sprint (2002) and Midget (2015) titles. He won 91 USAC national races, including 47 in sprint cars, and he won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons. Tracy Hines spent most of a quarter-century as a full-time competitor in all three USAC national divisions. He was the son of a New Castle, Indiana, midget racing family, and his father Jim and brother Ted were champions too. He later helped build other drivers' programs as a team executive. He broke through in 1996, winning his first National Midget race at Winchester in his first start back from a fiery crash. Hines won the Silver Crown title in 2000 and the Sprint title in 2002. In 2015, after announcing his retirement midseason, he won the Midget title and completed the Triple Crown. He scored 91 USAC national wins, including 47 in sprint cars, 35 in midgets and nine in Silver Crown. He won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons, 1996 through 2014. Away from USAC he raced in NASCAR's Truck and Busch series. USAC Triple Crown champion 2002 USAC Sprint champion 3 USAC titles 91 USAC national wins (47 Sprint) Triple Crown Tracy Hines, USAC.

body: Justin Grant is the all-time wins leader in USAC National Sprint Car racing, finishing the 2026 season with 71 series victories. He was the 2022 and 2023 USAC National Sprint Car champion, won Silver Crown titles in 2020 and 2025, and has won the USAC National Drivers championship five times. Justin Grant of Ione, California, built his record on durability. In July 2025 he set the record for consecutive USAC National Sprint starts, with 325, and he became the series' all-time wins leader. Grant was the 2010 USAC National Sprint Rookie of the Year. He won Silver Crown titles in 2020 and 2025 and National Sprint titles in 2022 and 2023. He has also won the National Drivers championship five times. In September 2025 at Lucas Oil Speedway he won his 63rd National Sprint feature, breaking Dave Darland's record, and that season he became the eighth driver with 100 USAC wins. He finished the 2026 season with 71 USAC National Sprint Car victories, his sixth and final 2026 win coming Aug. 29 at Kokomo. text: Northern Auto Racing Club (NARC). Brent Kaeding of Campbell, California, won a record 13 Northern Auto Racing Club (NARC) 410 sprint car championships, including eight in a row. He also won 13 Golden State Challenge titles, four Trophy Cups and the 1985 Turkey Night Grand Prix.…
body: Brent Kaeding of Campbell, California, won a record 13 Northern Auto Racing Club (NARC) 410 sprint car championships, including eight in a row. He also won 13 Golden State Challenge titles, four Trophy Cups and the 1985 Turkey Night Grand Prix. Brent Kaeding of Campbell, California, is the second of three generations of Northern California open-wheel champions. His father, Howard, raced modifieds and super modifieds, and his son Tim and nephew Bud also became top 410 sprint car drivers. Brent won his first NARC race at Silver Dollar Speedway in Chico in April 1981 and went on to win a record 13 NARC championships, including eight in a row. Over a career of more than three decades he won hundreds of features, an estimated 375 to more than 400, and he holds career win records at tracks from Chico to Tulare. title: Gary Wright “The Texan”
text: National Championship Racing Association (NCRA). Gary Wright won nine consecutive NCRA 410 sprint car championships from 1993 through 2001 and more than 75 NCRA features. The Texan later became the winningest driver in ASCS history with 128 National Tour wins and was inducted…
body: Gary Wright won nine consecutive NCRA 410 sprint car championships from 1993 through 2001 and more than 75 NCRA features. The Texan later became the winningest driver in ASCS history with 128 National Tour wins and was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2011. Gary Wright owned the NCRA 410 tour in the 1990s. The Texan won nine consecutive NCRA championships from 1993 through 2001 and more than 75 series features, taking over the series from his longtime friend and traveling companion Terry Gray. Wright then carried that dominance into the American Sprint Car Series, where he became the winningest driver in series history with 128 National Tour feature wins between 1994 and 2011 and four straight National Tour titles from 2004 through 2007. He also won with the All Star Circuit of Champions and the World of Outlaws, and his total career feature wins top 400. title: Terry Gray
text: National Championship Racing Association (NCRA). Terry Gray won NCRA 410 sprint car championships in 1989 and 1990 and led the series in wins in its first two seasons. The Bartlett, Tennessee, driver later won four ASCS and 16 USCS titles, entered the National Sprint Car Hall of…
body: Terry Gray won NCRA 410 sprint car championships in 1989 and 1990 and led the series in wins in its first two seasons. The Bartlett, Tennessee, driver later won four ASCS and 16 USCS titles, entered the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2022, and has said the 2026 Flip Flop 50 will be his final competition. Terry Gray of Bartlett, Tennessee, was the first star of the NCRA 410 tour after the series launched in 1988. The privateer, who began racing in 1974, already had a World of Outlaws feature win at Riverside Speedway in West Memphis, Arkansas, on Sept. 16, 1980, his only WoO victory. He led the NCRA in wins in its first two seasons and won the championship in 1989 and 1990. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2022. Gray later won four straight American Sprint Car Series National Tour titles from 1995 through 1998 and 16 USCS national championships. He earned his 99th career USCS feature win on Sept. 5, 2026, at Dixie Speedway in Woodstock, Georgia, and entered the 2026 Flip Flop 50 still at 99 wins. According to a Nov. 20, 2026, post from Riverside International Speedway, Gray said that USCS finale would be his final competition. body: Terry Gray of Bartlett, Tennessee, won four straight ASCS National Tour championships from 1995 through 1998, with 43 wins in those seasons. body: Jason Johnson, "The Ragin' Cajun," won five ASCS National Tour titles, then beat Donny Schatz for the 2016 Knoxville Nationals, one of the biggest upsets in the event's history. Jason Johnson of Eunice, Louisiana, was a 360 sprint car great on the ASCS National Tour. He won series titles in 2008, 2010, 2012, 2013 and 2014, and he and his wife, Bobbi, also won ASCS owner titles with Jason Johnson Racing. He moved to the World of Outlaws in 2015 and was the series Rookie of the Year. In 2016 he outdueled Donny Schatz to win the Knoxville Nationals, a win fans and historians remember as one of the biggest upsets in the event's history, second only to Bobby Allen's in 1990. He won 12 World of Outlaws features, the only Louisiana native to win in the series. title: Mel Kenyon “King of the Midgets”
text: USAC Midgets. Mel Kenyon, the "King of the Midgets," holds the USAC National Midget record with 111 feature wins and seven championships between 1964 and 1985. He won those races after losing the fingers of his left hand in a 1965 crash, and he made eight Indianapolis 500…
body: Mel Kenyon, the "King of the Midgets," holds the USAC National Midget record with 111 feature wins and seven championships between 1964 and 1985. He won those races after losing the fingers of his left hand in a 1965 crash, and he made eight Indianapolis 500 starts. Mel Kenyon and his brother Don built a family midget operation that set the standard in USAC National Midget racing. Don was his car owner and crew chief, and they also built their own chassis. From 2004 to 2009 their Kenyon Midget Series ran under USAC sanction. Mel won 111 USAC National Midget races, the series record. He won seven national championships over 21 years: 1964, 1967, 1968, 1974, 1977, 1981 and 1985. He also won at least one race in 21 straight seasons, 1962 through 1982. Most of that came after a fiery 1965 champ car crash at Langhorne that burned off the fingers of his left hand. The brothers designed a special glove that fit over a stud on the steering wheel so he could steer with his palm. Kenyon made eight Indianapolis 500 starts and finished in the top five in half of them, with a best of third in 1968. He retired in 2009 after more than 50 years of midget racing and 925 USAC National Midget starts. 111 USAC National Midget wins (record) 7 USAC National Midget titles 7 USAC Midget titles 111 USAC Midget wins (record) Mel Kenyon, USAC.

title: Rich Vogler
text: USAC Midgets. Rich Vogler won five USAC National Midget championships and the 1980 and 1989 USAC Sprint Car titles. His 95 National Midget wins rank second all-time, and he won the inaugural 1987 Chili Bowl and the Hut Hundred eight times. "Rapid Rich" Vogler of Glen Ellyn,…
body: Rich Vogler won five USAC National Midget championships and the 1980 and 1989 USAC Sprint Car titles. His 95 National Midget wins rank second all-time, and he won the inaugural 1987 Chili Bowl and the Hut Hundred eight times. "Rapid Rich" Vogler of Glen Ellyn, Illinois, the son of midget winner Don Vogler, was the most prolific winner of USAC's short-track era. In 1980 he became the first driver to win the USAC Sprint and Midget championships in the same year. He won five National Midget titles, in 1978, 1980, 1983, 1986 and 1988, and Sprint titles in 1980 and 1989. His 134 USAC national wins break down to 95 Midget, 35 Sprint and four Silver Crown. Only A.J. Foyt has more. Vogler won the Hut Hundred eight times and the 4-Crown midget race four times. He also won the inaugural Chili Bowl in 1987, and his 16 wins in 100-lap midget races are the most of anyone. He made five Indianapolis 500 starts, with a best of eighth in 1989. Vogler was killed on July 21, 1990, while leading a sprint car race at Salem Speedway, five days before his 40th birthday. Under USAC rules the race reverted to the last completed lap, so he was declared the winner of the last race he started. 95 USAC National Midget wins 1980 & 1989 USAC Sprint champion 7 USAC titles (5 Midget, 2 Sprint) 134 USAC national wins 8 Hut Hundreds 1 Chili Bowl Rich Vogler, USAC.

title: Bob Wente
text: USAC Midgets. Bob Wente was the 1963 USAC National Midget champion, and his 78 National Midget wins rank third all-time. He won the Hut Hundred and two Night Before the 500 races, finished ninth in the 1964 Indianapolis 500 and was in the inaugural Midget Hall of Fame class. Bob…
body: Bob Wente was the 1963 USAC National Midget champion, and his 78 National Midget wins rank third all-time. He won the Hut Hundred and two Night Before the 500 races, finished ninth in the 1964 Indianapolis 500 and was in the inaugural Midget Hall of Fame class. Bob Wente was a pillar of USAC midget racing's formative years, and he raised a family that kept racing midgets. All three of his sons competed in USAC Midget racing. He began racing midgets in 1954. He was runner-up in the national standings three years in a row before winning the 1963 USAC National Midget championship. Wente won 78 National Midget races, third all-time behind Mel Kenyon and Rich Vogler. He won the 1963 Hut Hundred and the Night Before the 500 in 1969 and 1976. In his only Indianapolis 500, in 1964, he started 32nd and finished ninth. He was in the inaugural class of the National Midget Auto Racing Hall of Fame in 1984. He died in 2000. 1963 USAC National Midget champion 78 National Midget wins Inaugural National Midget Hall of Fame class (1984) 1963 USAC Midget title 78 USAC Midget wins Bob Wente, USAC.

body: Kody Swanson holds the USAC Silver Crown records for championships, with eight, and wins, with 49. Those eight titles are the most any driver has won in a single USAC national series, and he also holds the series record of 59 poles, and he has won the Little 500 at Anderson Speedway four times (2016, 2018, 2019 and 2026). Kody Swanson of Kingsburg, California, has defined USAC Silver Crown racing for more than a decade. He set records in the series that may never be approached. He won the 2005 Western Sprint title and the 2009 Silver Crown Rookie of the Year award. He won his first Silver Crown title in 2014, and his eight titles (2014, 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2024) are the most any driver has won in a single USAC national series. His 49 Silver Crown wins and 59 poles are both series records by a wide margin. He won his eighth title in 2024 despite racing through an injury. He also won the 2017 Jason Leffler Award. On pavement, Swanson has won the Little 500 at Anderson Speedway four times, in 2016, 2018, 2019 and 2026, tying Tom Cherry for third on the event's all-time wins list. 8 USAC Silver Crown titles (record) 49 Silver Crown wins (record) 59 poles 4-time Little 500 winner (2016, 2018, 2019, 2026) 8 Silver Crown titles (record) 49 Silver Crown wins (record) 4 Little 500s (2016, 2018, 2019, 2026) Kody Swanson, 2024 USAC Silver Crown National Champion.

body: Jack Hewitt of Troy, Ohio, was the 1986 and 1987 USAC Silver Crown champion, and his 23 Silver Crown wins rank second all-time. In 1998 he swept all four features at Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals and raced in the Indianapolis 500. Jack Hewitt of Troy, Ohio, was the people's hero of Midwestern dirt racing. He was a racer's racer who would run anything, anywhere, and he was the son of racer Don Hewitt. He was a fan favorite as much for his personality as his driving. Blunt and outspoken, he never minced words, and fans loved him for it. He won Silver Crown titles in 1986 and 1987 and the 1985 All Star Circuit of Champions title. His 23 Silver Crown wins rank second all-time. He also won 46 USAC Sprint and seven Midget races. In 1998 he reached the Indianapolis 500 and finished 12th. That same year he swept all four features at Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals, in Silver Crown, Sprint, Midget and modified, for four different teams. In all he has won 19 4-Crown features, the most of anyone. He is a member of the USAC Hall of Fame. 2-time USAC Silver Crown champion 23 Silver Crown wins (2nd all-time) All Star Circuit of Champions champion Won the 1991 Grand Annual Sprintcar Classic at Warrnambool, Australia 2 Silver Crown titles 23 Silver Crown wins 19 4-Crown wins Crown jewel: 1991 Australian Classic Jack Hewitt in a USAC sprint car at Winchester, April 2, 1995.

body: Dave Steele of Tampa, Florida, won back-to-back USAC Silver Crown championships in 2004 and 2005 and was perhaps USAC's greatest pavement racer. All 60 of his USAC national wins came on asphalt: 16 in Silver Crown, 26 in sprint cars and 18 in midgets. Dave Steele of Tampa, Florida, may have been the greatest pavement racer in USAC history. All 60 of his USAC national wins, from 1996 to 2007, came on asphalt. He moved to the Midwest for the 1996 season. In his first USAC National Sprint start, at Lakeside Speedway, he swept the night: fastest qualifier, heat win and feature win. Steele won 16 Silver Crown, 26 Sprint and 18 Midget races, even though he usually ran half the schedule or less. He ran the full Silver Crown schedule in 2004 and 2005 and won the title both years. In 2002 he won two National Midget features in one night at Indianapolis Raceway Park, coming from 22nd in the second. He is a member of the USAC Hall of Fame. 2-time USAC Silver Crown champion 16 Silver Crown wins USAC Hall of Fame (2019) 2 Silver Crown titles 60 USAC national wins (16 Silver Crown) Dave Steele, USAC.

title: Pancho Carter
text: USAC Triple Crown. Pancho Carter was USAC's first career Triple Crown champion. He won the 1972 National Midget title, the 1974 and 1976 Sprint Car titles and the 1978 Silver Crown title. He also made 17 Indianapolis 500 starts, won the 1985 Indy pole and won the 1981 Michigan…
body: Pancho Carter was USAC's first career Triple Crown champion. He won the 1972 National Midget title, the 1974 and 1976 Sprint Car titles and the 1978 Silver Crown title. He also made 17 Indianapolis 500 starts, won the 1985 Indy pole and won the 1981 Michigan 500. Pancho Carter set the template for USAC versatility. The son of USAC Hall of Famer Duane Carter, he became the organization's first career Triple Crown champion and showed a generation of short-track drivers that one racer could master midgets, sprints and Silver Crown cars. He won the 1972 USAC National Midget title and Sprint Car titles in 1974 and 1976. In 1978 he won the Silver Crown title, then called the USAC National Dirt Championship. He scored 70 USAC national feature wins across those series. Carter was the 1974 Indianapolis 500 Rookie of the Year and made 17 Indy 500 starts. He won the pole in 1985 and finished third in 1982. He also won the 1981 Michigan 500. He is a member of both the National Sprint Car and National Midget Halls of Fame and the USAC Hall of Fame. title: Tony Stewart
text: USAC Triple Crown. Tony Stewart is the first driver to win all three USAC national championships in one season, sweeping the Midget, Sprint and Silver Crown titles in 1995. He won the 1997 IndyCar title and three NASCAR Cup championships (2002, 2005 and 2011). As a car owner he…
body: Tony Stewart is the first driver to win all three USAC national championships in one season, sweeping the Midget, Sprint and Silver Crown titles in 1995. He won the 1997 IndyCar title and three NASCAR Cup championships (2002, 2005 and 2011). As a car owner he has nine World of Outlaws titles with Danny Lasoski and Donny Schatz, the 2026 High Limit title with Rico Abreu, seven USAC Sprint and seven Silver Crown owner championships, two NASCAR Cup and two Xfinity owner titles, and the 2023 NHRA Funny Car title. The Columbus, Indiana, driver won the 1994 USAC National Midget title. In 1995 he won the Midget, Sprint and Silver Crown championships, the first driver ever to sweep all three in a single season. He won 27 USAC National Midget races, 10 Sprint races and three Silver Crown races. Stewart won the 1997 Indy Racing League title and started on the pole for the 1996 Indianapolis 500. He then won three NASCAR Cup championships as a driver, in 2002, 2005 and 2011, the last as an owner-driver for Stewart-Haas Racing. He is the only driver to win championships in both IndyCar and NASCAR. He also won the Brickyard 400 in 2005 and 2007, the Chili Bowl Midget Nationals in 2002 and 2007, and the 2006 IROC championship. As a car owner, his record is separate from those driving titles. Tony Stewart Racing won nine World of Outlaws Sprint Car owner championships: the first with Danny Lasoski in 2001, in the team's inaugural season after Stewart formed TSR in November 2000, and eight more with Donny Schatz in 2008, 2009, 2012 and 2014 through 2018. Schatz joined TSR for the 2008 season after winning the 2006 and 2007 Outlaws titles with his own Donny Schatz Motorsports team. He and TSR parted ways on August 12, 2025, during a winless season; Kerry Madsen finished 2025 in the No. 15. TSR has not won another World of Outlaws title since Schatz's last one in 2018 (Brad Sweet won the series in 2020 and 2022). In 2026, after that split, Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing won the High Limit Racing owner title with Rico Abreu, Abreu's second straight High Limit driving championship and Stewart's first as a High Limit owner; Abreu's 2025 High Limit title was with his own team. Official USAC entrant-champion records credit Stewart with seven National Sprint Car owner titles and seven Silver Crown owner titles. The Sprint titles were with J.J. Yeley (2003), Josh Wise (2006) and Levi Jones (2007, 2009, 2010 and 2011), and Bryan Clauson (2013). The Silver Crown titles were with Yeley (2002 and 2003) and Dave Steele (2004 and 2005) under East-Stewart Racing, co-owned with Bob East, then with Jones (2010 and 2011) and Bobby East (2013) under Tony Stewart Racing / Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing. Two often-cited years are not official Stewart owner titles: Jay Drake won the 2004 Sprint driver championship in a TSR car, but the USAC Sprint entrant title that year went to Dynamics, Inc. #69; Bobby East won the 2012 Silver Crown driver championship in a TSR car, but the official entrant title that year went to RW Motorsports/Curb-Agajanian Racing #17. Stewart-Haas Racing added NASCAR Cup owner championships in 2011, with Stewart driving, and in 2014 with Kevin Harvick. SHR also won two NASCAR Xfinity Series owner championships with Cole Custer in the No. 00: the 2018 owners title (Custer finished second in driver points to Tyler Reddick) and the 2023 title, when Custer also won the driver championship. SHR did not win a NASCAR Truck Series owner championship. In 2023 Matt Hagan won the NHRA Funny Car world championship for Tony Stewart Racing, the team's first NHRA title. In 2024 Stewart drove the team's Top Fuel dragster himself, reached two final rounds, made the Countdown to the Championship and was named NHRA Rookie of the Year. He was inducted into the National Midget Hall of Fame in 2001, the USAC Hall of Fame in 2016, the Motorsports Hall of Fame of America in 2019, the NASCAR Hall of Fame in 2020 and the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2022. Driver: 1995 single-season USAC Triple Crown (Midget, Sprint, Silver Crown); 1994 National Midget title Driver: 1997 Indy Racing League champion; 1996 Indianapolis 500 pole Driver: 3 NASCAR Cup titles (2002, 2005, 2011, the last as owner-driver) Driver: Brickyard 400 wins in 2005 and 2007; Chili Bowl Nationals wins in 2002 and 2007; 2006 IROC champion Owner: 9 World of Outlaws titles — Danny Lasoski (2001) and Donny Schatz (2008, 2009, 2012, 2014–18); Schatz joined TSR in 2008 and left Aug. 12, 2025 Owner: 2026 High Limit Racing title with Rico Abreu (Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing) Owner: 7 USAC National Sprint titles — Yeley (2003), Wise (2006), Jones (2007, 2009–11), Clauson (2013) Owner: 7 USAC Silver Crown titles — Yeley (2002–03) and Steele (2004–05) with East-Stewart Racing; Jones (2010–11) and Bobby East (2013) Owner: 2 NASCAR Cup titles with Stewart-Haas Racing (2011 with Stewart, 2014 with Kevin Harvick) Owner: 2 NASCAR Xfinity titles with Stewart-Haas Racing and Cole Custer (2018 owners championship; 2023 driver and owner title) Owner: 2023 NHRA Funny Car world title with Matt Hagan Driver: 1995 USAC Triple Crown Driver: 1997 IndyCar title Driver: 3 NASCAR Cup titles (2002, 2005, 2011) Owner: 9 WoO titles (Lasoski 2001; Schatz 2008–09, 2012, 2014–18) Owner: 2026 High Limit title (Abreu) Owner: 7 USAC Sprint and 7 Silver Crown titles Owner: 2 NASCAR Cup titles (2011 Stewart, 2014 Harvick) Owner: 2 NASCAR Xfinity titles (2018, 2023 Custer) Owner: 2023 NHRA Funny Car title (Hagan) Tony Stewart, World of Outlaws.

title: Dave Darland “The People's Champ”
text: USAC Triple Crown. Dave Darland, the "People's Champ," is a USAC Triple Crown champion with titles in Silver Crown (1997), Sprint (1999) and Midget (2001–02). He retired in 2023 with 62 USAC National Sprint Car wins, then the record, and a record 20 Indiana Sprint Week wins.…
body: Dave Darland, the "People's Champ," is a USAC Triple Crown champion with titles in Silver Crown (1997), Sprint (1999) and Midget (2001–02). He retired in 2023 with 62 USAC National Sprint Car wins, then the record, and a record 20 Indiana Sprint Week wins. Dave Darland was USAC's everyman champion. Fans called him the "People's Champ." Over nearly four decades he made more USAC national starts than anyone, 1,334, and he showed that a local Indiana sprint car racer could become one of the sport's all-time greats. Born in 1966 in Lincoln, Indiana, he won four national titles: Silver Crown in 1997, Sprint in 1999, and Midget in 2001 and 2002. That made him the third career Triple Crown champion. His 62 USAC National Sprint Car wins were the record when he retired in 2023. His 20 Indiana Sprint Week wins are still the most of any driver. He won 115 USAC features nationally and regionally, including 30 National Midget and 14 Silver Crown wins. He won at least one USAC national feature in a record 24 straight seasons, 1993 through 2016. Along the way he won Turkey Night, the midget classic, twice. Darland is a member of the USAC Hall of Fame. body: J.J. Yeley swept all three USAC national championships in 2003, joining Tony Stewart as the only single-season Triple Crown winners. His 24 USAC wins that year broke A.J. Foyt's single-season record, and he also won the 2001 Sprint and 2002 Silver Crown titles. J.J. Yeley's 2003 season remains the high-water mark for a USAC driver. Racing Tony Stewart's sprint and Silver Crown cars and the Steve Lewis midget Stewart had driven in 1995, he won all three national championships and 24 USAC races. That broke the single-season record of 19 set by A.J. Foyt. Yeley won Indiana Sprint Week and USAC Sprint Rookie of the Year in 1997. He finished ninth in the 1998 Indianapolis 500 despite a first-lap spin. After an IndyCar run in 2000, he returned to USAC. He won the Sprint title in 2001, the Silver Crown title in 2002, and then the 2003 sweep, joining Stewart as the only drivers to win the Triple Crown in a single season. He moved to NASCAR with Joe Gibbs Racing in 2004 and has raced in the national touring series ever since. 2003 single-season USAC Triple Crown 5 USAC titles 24 USAC wins in 2003 Single-season Triple Crown J.J. body: Jerry Coons Jr. of Tucson, Arizona, is a USAC Triple Crown champion. He won the National Midget titles in 2006 and 2007, then both the Sprint and Silver Crown titles in 2008. He was USAC's Midget Driver of the Decade for 2000–09 and the first three-time winner of the Belleville Midget Nationals. Jerry Coons Jr. brought Arizona into USAC's elite. The Tucson driver made his National Midget debut in 1987 and has 430 series starts, among the most ever, and he became one of USAC's most respected veterans. His first National Midget win came at the 1996 Belleville Midget Nationals. He later became the first three-time winner of that race, in 2005, 2007 and 2012. Coons won the National Midget championship in 2006 and 2007. In 2008 he won both the Sprint and Silver Crown titles to complete the career Triple Crown. USAC named him National Midget Driver of the Decade for 2000–09. At Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals he won in all three USAC divisions: Silver Crown in 2007 and 2014, Sprint in 2009 and Midget in 2010. title: Tracy Hines
text: USAC Triple Crown. Tracy Hines is a USAC Triple Crown champion with Silver Crown (2000), Sprint (2002) and Midget (2015) titles. He won 91 USAC national races, including 47 in sprint cars, and he won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons. Tracy Hines spent most of…
body: Tracy Hines is a USAC Triple Crown champion with Silver Crown (2000), Sprint (2002) and Midget (2015) titles. He won 91 USAC national races, including 47 in sprint cars, and he won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons. Tracy Hines spent most of a quarter-century as a full-time competitor in all three USAC national divisions. He was the son of a New Castle, Indiana, midget racing family, and his father Jim and brother Ted were champions too. He later helped build other drivers' programs as a team executive. He broke through in 1996, winning his first National Midget race at Winchester in his first start back from a fiery crash. Hines won the Silver Crown title in 2000 and the Sprint title in 2002. In 2015, after announcing his retirement midseason, he won the Midget title and completed the Triple Crown. He scored 91 USAC national wins, including 47 in sprint cars, 35 in midgets and nine in Silver Crown. He won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons, 1996 through 2014. Away from USAC he raced in NASCAR's Truck and Busch series. USAC Triple Crown champion 2002 USAC Sprint champion 3 USAC titles 91 USAC national wins (47 Sprint) Triple Crown Tracy Hines, USAC.

body: Chris Windom became USAC's seventh Triple Crown champion with the 2016 Silver Crown, 2017 National Sprint and 2020 National Midget titles. The Canton, Illinois, driver is also a two-time Little 500 and two-time Indiana Sprint Week winner. Chris Windom of Canton, Illinois, showed how far a family-run program could go in USAC. He won the Little 500 in 2011 and again in 2015. He won the Silver Crown title in 2016 and the National Sprint title in 2017. In 2020 he won the National Midget title and became the seventh career Triple Crown champion. Windom won Indiana Sprint Week in 2011 and 2018, the Eastern Storm in 2017 and 2018. He has also raced stock cars, including the 2021 NASCAR Cup race on the Bristol dirt, and in recent seasons he has moved toward winged sprint car racing. body: Logan Seavey became USAC's eighth Triple Crown champion when he added the 2024 National Sprint title to his 2023 Silver Crown and his 2018 and 2023 National Midget titles. He did it with Abacus Racing, which won owner titles in all three divisions. Logan Seavey of Sutter, California, and Abacus Racing built one of USAC's most complete modern programs. In 2023 he won both the Silver Crown and National Midget titles. He added the 2024 Sprint title, along with Indiana Sprint Week and the National Drivers championship, to become the eighth career Triple Crown champion. body: Kenny Weld was the first four-time Knoxville Nationals winner and the man to beat in Pennsylvania in the early 1970s. He later made his mark as a builder. Kenny Weld grew up in a Kansas City racing family. At 18 he won the 1964 Knoxville Nationals, and he won again in 1965, 1972 and 1973 to become the event's first four-time winner. Driving the Weikert Livestock Special in Pennsylvania, he won 43 features in 1973 and a record fifth straight Williams Grove track title in 1974. He is credited with 189 feature wins between 1967 and 1975. After driving he became a builder, from the dirt modified "Batmobile" to Weld Tech. He died in 1997, the year he entered the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame. body: Jan Opperman was one of the original outlaws, a long-haired racer who chased the best-paying shows across the country. He won the 1971 Knoxville Nationals and 44 features in 1972, and his charisma made him one of the most beloved drivers in the sport. Jan Opperman was one of the original outlaws. Discovered in California in 1968, he raced anywhere that paid, which kept him from piling up records with any one sanctioning body. He won the 1971 Knoxville Nationals and the Western World Championship that same season, then won 44 features in 1972. In 1976 he won the Hulman Classic at Terre Haute. He also co-designed the Maxwell sprint car and made two Indianapolis 500 starts. With long hair and a charisma few others had, he was one of the most beloved drivers in the sport and a big draw everywhere he raced. Crashes in 1976 and 1981 cut his career short. title: Jac Haudenschild “The Wild Child”
text: Old School Legends. Jac Haudenschild, "The Wild Child," was the most fearless driver in World of Outlaws history. He won 72 series features and three Kings Royals, and fans never took their eyes off him. Pronounced HOWD-en-shield, Jac Haudenschild's last name tripped up…
body: Jac Haudenschild, "The Wild Child," was the most fearless driver in World of Outlaws history. He won 72 series features and three Kings Royals, and fans never took their eyes off him. Pronounced HOWD-en-shield, Jac Haudenschild's last name tripped up announcers for years, and the mispronunciations gave way to the nickname "The Wild Child," one that fit his fearless driving style perfectly. The Wooster, Ohio, driver was the most daring the World of Outlaws ever saw, and his signature run around the outer edge of the speedway became known as the Haud Line. Even from ninth or 10th he could amaze a crowd, and he never burned a bridge, driving for 14 different winning car owners in the series. He won 72 World of Outlaws features, from the 1982 Eldora Nationals to his last series win at Eldora in 2010. His best points finish was second in 1995. He won the Kings Royal three times (1987, 1994, 1998), the Gold Cup three times and the 2003 Mopar Million. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2009 while still racing, and ran his final race at the 2021 World Finals. His son, Sheldon Haudenschild, has continued that exciting legacy, thrilling a new generation of fans on the Haud Line, a line that was clearly in his DNA. 72 World of Outlaws wins Kings Royal: 1987, 1994, 1998 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (2009) 72 WoO wins Crown jewel: 3 Kings Royals Jac Haudenschild with his son Sheldon Haudenschild (cropped to Jac), World of Outlaws.

title: Bobby Allen “Scruffy”
text: Old School Legends. Bobby Allen did a lot with a little. In 1990 the low-budget racer drove his homebuilt No. 1a past Sammy Swindell to win the Knoxville Nationals, still remembered as the biggest upset in the event's history. Bobby Allen grew up in Miami racing go-karts, then…
body: Bobby Allen did a lot with a little. In 1990 the low-budget racer drove his homebuilt No. 1a past Sammy Swindell to win the Knoxville Nationals, still remembered as the biggest upset in the event's history. Bobby Allen grew up in Miami racing go-karts, then headed to Pennsylvania as a teenager because that was where the sprint cars ran three and four nights a week. He became one of the sport's original outlaws. He was known for doing a lot with a little. He built his own chassis, put together his own engines and made his own setup calls on the familiar No. 1a, spending what money he had on the car rather than on how it looked. On Aug. 18, 1990, in front of about 18,000 fans, his homebuilt car beat the well-funded Sammy Swindell to win the Knoxville Nationals. It is remembered as the biggest upset in the event's history. He won more than 275 sprint car features, including 30 with the World of Outlaws and 46 with the All Star Circuit of Champions, where he won the 1980 title. He entered the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 1988. He later owned Shark Racing of Hanover, Pa., and in 2014 took the team on the World of Outlaws tour full time with his grandson, Logan Schuchart, and his son, Jacob Allen. Jacob drove the team's No. 1A until he stepped away from full-time driving in April 2025. After a three-race stint by Cale Thomas, Ashton Torgerson took over the seat later that month, and Jacob stayed on to run the No. 1A as crew chief. Bobby Allen died Oct. 5, 2025, at 81. 1990 Knoxville Nationals winner 30 World of Outlaws wins 1980 All Star Circuit of Champions champion National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (1988) 30 WoO wins Crown jewel: 1990 Knoxville Nationals Bobby Allen at Hagerstown, May 24, 1987, World of Outlaws.

title: Brad Doty
text: Old School Legends. Brad Doty was a World of Outlaws winner and 1987 points runner-up whose driving career ended in the 1988 Kings Royal. He stayed in the sport as a promoter and its best-known TV analyst, and fans have never stopped loving him for it. Brad Doty of Ohio was…
body: Brad Doty was a World of Outlaws winner and 1987 points runner-up whose driving career ended in the 1988 Kings Royal. He stayed in the sport as a promoter and its best-known TV analyst, and fans have never stopped loving him for it. Brad Doty of Ohio was World of Outlaws and Knoxville Nationals Rookie of the Year in 1982. He won 18 World of Outlaws features and 73 sprint car features in all, and he finished second to Steve Kinser in the 1987 World of Outlaws standings. A crash on the opening lap of the 1988 Kings Royal at Eldora left him paralyzed from the chest down. He never left the sport. He started the Brad Doty Classic in 1989 and from 1992 became the best-known television voice of winged sprint car racing. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2001. 1982 World of Outlaws Rookie of the Year 18 World of Outlaws wins 1987 World of Outlaws runner-up National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (2001) 18 WoO wins 73 career feature wins Brad Doty at Attica, July 14, 2020, World of Outlaws.
